comparisons.reason: Its defining ability is coordinated impact tool use and hand withdrawal, not continuous torque balance during adjustment and locking.

comparisons.objective: Remove the internal burr from a cut copper tube without over-chamfering it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold the tube against cutting torque, coaxially seat a reamer, make controlled rotary strokes, and repeatedly regrasp it.
comparisons.success_condition: Every bore sector receives the required passes without excessive chamfer, and the tube and reamer are returned and released.
comparisons.reason: It shares coaxial tool seating, regrasping, and reaction torque, but tests controlled material removal while holding a workpiece rather than preserving a screw setting during jam-nut lock and subsequent actuation.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks an assembled gripper’s opening stop; PR-2251 installs and electrically engages a T8 tube in two rotor lampholders.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests concentric two-tool screw/nut counterholding and later lever actuation; PR-2251 tests bimanual support of a long fragile tube, simultaneous dual-end pin insertion, and coordinated quarter-turn rotation.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a retained 90° opening across three cycles with limited drift, retained nuts, and withdrawn tools; PR-2251 requires both pin pairs inserted, both rotors at their 90° stops, illumination, release, and one-second stillness.
comparisons.reason: Although both involve angular regulation and functional verification, dual-end lamp insertion and rotation do not exercise coupled screw-and-locknut adjustment under countertorque; no material comparison rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Seat a strain-wave flexspline unit into a robot-joint housing with its teeth meshed.
comparisons.physical_skill: Align two axes, rotate to tooth phase while applying insertion force, avoid cocking, and release after seating.
comparisons.success_condition: The collar is within 0.5 mm of the housing face, teeth are meshed, alignment tolerances hold, and the unit remains still after release.
comparisons.reason: This robot-assembly task tests turn-to-mesh precision insertion, not two-tool threaded adjustment, countertorque locking, or repeated motion retention.

comparisons.objective: Replace a blown DIN-rail fuse with the correctly rated spare and relatch the named holder.
comparisons.physical_skill: Open a small carrier, extract and sort a cartridge, insert the correct replacement, and close a latch without disturbing neighbors.
comparisons.success_condition: F2 contains the correct fuse, the failed fuse is in the tray, and the carrier withstands a pull test; wrong-rating or wrong-holder actions score zero.
comparisons.reason: Its core is target selection and small-part replacement in a hinged carrier, not calibration-preserving threaded locking.

comparisons.objective: Fasten a screw through an upright plate into a coupling nut held on the far side.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually align separate screw and nut, hold the nut against rotation, catch the thread, and turn the screw until snug.
comparisons.success_condition: The screw passes through the plate, engages for at least 1.5 turns, and leaves both head and nut snug after release.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest generic fastening primitive, but it creates a new screw-nut joint to a snug endpoint; the candidate preserves an existing adjustable stop against jam-nut reaction and must prove its setting through repeated actuation.

comparisons.objective: Drive a curved suture needle through a practice pad along its arc and hand it to the other gripper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Rotate a curved needle about its center, avoid lateral tissue loading, grasp the emerging section, and execute a controlled handoff.
comparisons.success_condition: The needle traverses both slots without tearing or pad contact, the second hand holds it, and the first releases it while it remains threaded.
comparisons.reason: This tests curved-path insertion and in-place handoff, unrelated to threaded adjustment, counterholding, and lock retention.

comparisons.objective: Use a plumb bob to transfer a shelf-hole position onto a worktop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Damp a pendulum by touch, release it without re-excitation, and mark accurately in a narrow clearance while it hangs freely.
comparisons.success_condition: All pencil marks are made while the bob is free and still and lie within 3 mm of plumb, with the pencil lifted afterward.
comparisons.reason: Its defining ability is dynamic pendulum damping followed by precision marking, not tool-mediated mechanical adjustment and locking.

comparisons.objective: Fit a smartphone into a hybrid case in the correct orientation and snap all corners under the lip.
comparisons.physical_skill: Orient a thin fragile object, align an asymmetric camera feature, and sequentially press corners through compliant latches.
comparisons.success_condition: All four corners are seated under the lip with the phone correctly oriented and the case flat, released, and still.
comparisons.reason: This is compliant snap-fit insertion with orientation constraints, not threaded countertorque or functional setting verification.

comparisons.objective: Mark a banknote with a counterfeit pen while pinning it, then sort it according to the mark.
comparisons.physical_skill: Stabilize an extremely light sheet against pen drag, draw a controlled stroke, return the pen, and slide the note without lifting it.
comparisons.success_condition: A valid pinned stroke is made, the pen is returned, and the note is released flat on the correct result mat without prohibited ink or smearing.
comparisons.reason: It tests sheet stabilization during marking and result-based sorting rather than coupled mechanical adjustment and locking.

comparisons.objective: Connect a mop frame's swiveling socket to its handle until the spring button clicks.
comparisons.physical_skill: Counterpose an articulated socket, coaxially align a long handle, push through spring resistance, and engage a keyed lug and button.
comparisons.success_condition: The lug bottoms in its notch, the spring button protrudes through the window, and the assembled mop is released and still.
comparisons.reason: It tests alignment and forceful snap-latch insertion of two long parts, not maintaining an angular screw setting while tightening a concentric locknut.

comparisons.objective: Extinguish a nearby candle before safely packing a vase into a box.
comparisons.physical_skill: Place a bell snuffer over a wick without moving the chamberstick, then transfer and place a fragile vase.
comparisons.success_condition: The flame is extinguished before packing, the candle holder never exceeds movement limits, and the vase is upright, released, and still in the box.
comparisons.reason: This is hazard sequencing plus careful placement, with no adjustable threaded mechanism or retention-under-cycle requirement.

comparisons.objective: Candidate configures and locks a gripper motion limit; PR-2252 refits and latches a heavy range-hood baffle filter.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires seated driver/wrench coordination that prevents a screw setting from drifting during nut tightening; PR-2252 requires carrying an awkward slab, seating its bottom edge in a trough, swinging it flush, and operating a spring latch.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades target opening, lock retention, repeated motion, drift, hardware retention, and final clearance; PR-2252 grades trough engagement, flush seating, latch return over the filter, release, and one-second stability.
comparisons.reason: PR-2252’s placement-and-latching outcome does not test torque-coupled adjustment preservation or repeated functional retention; no material comparison rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Sort colored cubes while responding to a high-level alarm by closing a tank inlet before overflow.
comparisons.physical_skill: Monitor a timed process, interrupt a sorting task, operate a sliding valve, and resume manipulation.
comparisons.success_condition: All cubes are correctly sorted and the valve is closed after the alarm but before overflow and remains closed; overflow scores zero.
comparisons.reason: Its tested difficulty is event-timed task switching and valve operation, not precision mechanical calibration and locknut counterholding.

comparisons.objective: Rinse a glass on a push-down bar rinser and leave it draining on a mat.
comparisons.physical_skill: Invert and center a glass, depress a spring-loaded plate while maintaining coverage, then transport and place the glass rim-down.
comparisons.success_condition: The rinser is covered and depressed for 1.5 seconds and the glass is released, stable, and rim-down on the drip mat without unsafe spraying.
comparisons.reason: This tests spring-loaded appliance actuation and glass placement, unrelated to threaded setting preservation and jam-nut locking.

comparisons.objective: Install safety caps on exposed rebar stubs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Pick up bulky caps, coaxially align blind bores over bars, and push them down far enough to engage gripping fins.
comparisons.success_condition: All five bars have fully seated, retained caps and both robot tools remain clear for three seconds; dislodged caps revoke credit.
comparisons.reason: This is repeated axial press-fit insertion and retention, not rotational adjustment with coupled screw-and-nut countertorque or functional cycling.

comparisons.objective: Free a tote strap ring from a rake tine, then move the tote from shelf to table.
comparisons.physical_skill: Unhooking an articulated strap without dragging the rake, followed by bimanual tote transport.
comparisons.success_condition: Ring off every tine; rake remains safely on the shelf; tote upright, released, and still on the table.
comparisons.reason: Tests entanglement removal and transport, not precise screw adjustment, jam-nut counterlocking, or retained articulated cycling.

comparisons.objective: Place caplets in the correct pill-organizer cells and snap every lid shut.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold down a light organizer while lifting small catches, placing pills, and re-latching lids.
comparisons.success_condition: Exactly one caplet in Monday and Thursday, no dosing errors, all lids snapped, organizer released and stable.
comparisons.reason: Tests small-lid unlatching, placement, and snapping; it has no adjustable stop, coupled screw/nut locking, or setting-retention verification.

comparisons.objective: Magnetically attach a stylus to a tablet and lift the tablet from a flush tabletop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Magnetic face alignment, creation of thin-object grasp access, and attachment-preserving lift.
comparisons.success_condition: Stylus correctly attached and unsupported by a hand while the tablet is held at least 50 mm above the desk for five seconds.
comparisons.reason: Tests magnetic alignment and flat-object pickup rather than countertorque, locknut tightening, and repeatable stop-angle retention.

comparisons.objective: Form a two-bend 45-degree offset in tubing and place it on a template.
comparisons.physical_skill: Repositioning tube through a hand bender, making opposite irreversible bends, and compensating for springback.
comparisons.success_condition: Two acceptable bends, parallel ends at the specified offset, released on the template and still; over-bending or same-direction bends fail.
comparisons.reason: Tests material forming and springback across two bends, not adjustment of an existing mechanism followed by jam-nut locking and functional cycles.

comparisons.objective: Elicit a knee-jerk response with a reflex hammer and put the hammer down safely.
comparisons.physical_skill: Fast, accurately located impact followed by prompt lift-off and tool placement.
comparisons.success_condition: A sufficiently strong kick from a valid brisk tendon strike, then hammer released in its cup or on the bench and still.
comparisons.reason: Tests dynamic striking speed, impact location, and lift-off rather than coupled rotary adjustment and retention.

comparisons.objective: Deploy an attached folding support and leave a tablet standing for hands-free viewing.
comparisons.physical_skill: Manipulating thin hinged panels, coordinating an attached assembly, and transferring load to a stable support.
comparisons.success_condition: Tablet released near the required portrait tilt, supported by its edge and stand, and stable for five seconds.
comparisons.reason: Although both involve articulated motion and released verification, this tests support deployment and load transfer, not preserving a screw setting while locking a jam nut.

comparisons.objective: Press a weatherstrip-loaded door shut and throw its deadbolt.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual sustained door restraint while pinching and rotating a thumb-turn.
comparisons.success_condition: Bolt substantially extended into the strike while the door remains shut and stable for one second.
comparisons.reason: Shares generic stabilization-plus-turning, but tests maintaining door alignment against spring force while throwing a bolt, not concentric screw/nut countertorque, calibrated adjustment, or cycle retention.

comparisons.objective: Present a calibration checkerboard in the views needed for camera calibration, then return it to its rack.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual board handling with precise pose coverage, visibility control, and steady holds.
comparisons.success_condition: All positional, scale, and skew views detected; focal length recovered within tolerance; board returned, released, and still.
comparisons.reason: Tests multi-view visual target presentation and calibration observability, with no threaded setting or locking operation.

comparisons.objective: Load washable blender components into a dishwasher while excluding the motor base.
comparisons.physical_skill: Semantic object selection and collision-safe placement of a jug and lid in a rack.
comparisons.success_condition: Jug and lid separately released and stable inside the rack; motor entry permanently fails the task.
comparisons.reason: Tests selective sorting and placement, not dexterous adjustment, counterlocking, or post-lock functional verification.

comparisons.objective: Clamp an edge-glued panel with three clamps alternating above and below.
comparisons.physical_skill: Place a clamp, close multiple sliding jaws, regulate clamping force, and maintain panel alignment.
comparisons.success_condition: Joint closed and level with three snug alternating clamps; excessive force permanently fails; hands clear and assembly still.
comparisons.reason: Tests distributed force application and clamp layout, not locking a rotary adjustment without disturbing it or checking repeated actuator return.

comparisons.objective: Tear the front panel from a loaded shelf-ready tray along its perforations.
comparisons.physical_skill: Restrain a heavy tray while directing a controlled peel/tear along designed lines.
comparisons.success_condition: Panel fully removed on the perforation without tray displacement, tipping, product loss, or residual panel; released and still.
comparisons.reason: Tests controlled tearing of packaging under reaction load, not threaded adjustment or lock retention.

comparisons.objective: Slit a carton's taped seam without damaging the product, then retract the cutter blade.
comparisons.physical_skill: Deploy a blade and control its angle, depth, and path over a long cut.
comparisons.success_condition: Tape completely slit, product and cardboard outside the tape undamaged, blade retracted, and carton not tipped.
comparisons.reason: Tests guarded cutting-depth control and tool-state restoration, not bimanual rotary counterlocking or repeated mechanism actuation.

comparisons.objective: Open a casement window to the last peg-stay hole and secure it there.
comparisons.physical_skill: Lift a stay clear of intermediate holes while moving the sash, then lower the correct hole over a pin.
comparisons.success_condition: Last hole captured on the pin, hands clear, sash and stay still; glass intrusion or an unsecured stay fails.
comparisons.reason: Tests coordinated articulated repositioning and hole-on-pin capture, not tool-driven screw adjustment or torque-preserving lockup.

comparisons.objective: Load an anaesthetic cartridge into a dental syringe and engage its harpoon safely.
comparisons.physical_skill: Orient and insert a fragile cartridge, align a small harpoon with a stopper, and apply bounded axial force.
comparisons.success_condition: Cartridge correctly oriented in the barrel, harpoon passes an aspiration test, syringe rests correctly, and excessive stopper travel never occurs.
comparisons.reason: Tests fragile insertion and controlled barb engagement rather than rotary setpoint adjustment, jam-nut locking, and repeated stop verification.

comparisons.objective: Separate the halves of a side-release buckle.
comparisons.physical_skill: Simultaneously depress two sprung tabs while restraining the light halves and pulling them apart.
comparisons.success_condition: Both tabs actuated and the male tongue fully withdrawn; falling off the table fails.
comparisons.reason: Tests concurrent latch release and extraction, with no adjustable setting, threaded countertorque, or retained-cycle outcome.

comparisons.objective: Install three culture-tube caps at their vented first detent rather than the sealed second detent.
comparisons.physical_skill: Coaxially align small caps and regulate insertion depth/force to stop at an intermediate click.
comparisons.success_condition: All three caps upright, centered, released, still, and within the first-stop height band; over-seating does not count.
comparisons.reason: It shares precise intermediate-state control, but tests axial snap-detent seating on separate tubes. It does not lock a continuous screw adjustment with a jam nut or verify that setting through articulated cycles.

comparisons.objective: Unscrew a flashlight tail cap, remove its battery into a bin, and set the parts down.
comparisons.physical_skill: Counterhold a cylindrical body, turn a threaded cap through a full release, tip out an internal cell, and place components.
comparisons.success_condition: Cap genuinely unscrewed and placed safely, battery in the box, flashlight returned outside it, all released and still.
comparisons.reason: Shares bimanual counterholding and threaded rotation, but its tested outcome is disassembly and extraction. It does not preserve a calibrated screw position while tightening a concentric jam nut or demonstrate retained motion.

comparisons.objective: Configure a meter test switch safely and insert a current test plug.
comparisons.physical_skill: Manipulate multiple guarded knife switches and align a flat probe with spring contacts while respecting electrical interlocks.
comparisons.success_condition: Specified voltage and phase-A switches open safely, plug seated and retained under a push-back check; unsafe switch states score zero.
comparisons.reason: Tests ordered interlocked switching and electrical-test-plug insertion, not mechanical angle adjustment and counterlocked retention.

comparisons.objective: Lift a sagging replacement pipe into line and slide a repair coupling across its joint.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual pipe alignment and close-clearance sleeve translation while the pipe pivots in an elbow.
comparisons.success_condition: Coupling centered with sufficient insertion on both pipes, replacement aligned and home, hands clear, and assembly still.
comparisons.reason: Tests coaxial support and translational insertion; it has no threaded setpoint, jam-nut locking, or repeated actuation check.

comparisons.objective: Remove a flush glass pane using two suction lifters and place it on bearers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Position and lock two suction tools, coordinate a level bimanual lift, then unlock them after placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Pane lifted with both lifters, laid flat on bearers, lifters unlocked, hands clear, and no drop, excessive tilt, or direct gripper contact.
comparisons.reason: Tests attachment-tool setup, cooperative fragile-sheet transport, and release, not rotary adjustment with locknut countertorque and retained-cycle verification.

comparisons.objective: Remove snapped filament from a printer extruder and discard it while restoring the tension lever.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold a spring lever open while the other hand pulls a thin filament through the released drive nip.
comparisons.success_condition: Filament is removed and placed in the tray, lever restored, and arms withdrawn; partial credit tracks extraction distance.
comparisons.reason: Concurrent hold-and-pull shares generic bimanual coordination but lacks coaxial tool seating, screw adjustment, jam-nut countertorque, and retained-angle verification.

comparisons.objective: Grind a measured batch of peppercorns to specified coarse and fine mass fractions.
comparisons.physical_skill: Apply sustained downward force and circular or impact pestle motion while containing material.
comparisons.success_condition: Specified sieve fractions are reached with limited loss and the pestle safely released.
comparisons.reason: Grinding and granular containment do not exercise coupled screw/nut adjustment, countertorque, or retained articulated motion.

comparisons.objective: Re-space two gondola wire dividers to prescribed planogram holes without disturbing stocked boxes.
comparisons.physical_skill: Lift and align each long divider so its rear foot enters a small hole while its front hook captures a fence wire.
comparisons.success_condition: Both feet and hooks occupy the target pitches, products remain upright, and grippers clear the shelf.
comparisons.reason: This is simultaneous two-end alignment and seating of shelf accessories, not tool-mediated angular adjustment and locknut retention.

comparisons.objective: Turn a cake out of its pan onto a plate and remove the pan.
comparisons.physical_skill: Clamp a broad plate-pan stack from opposite sides, lift and rotate it cooperatively, then separate the pan.
comparisons.success_condition: The inverted cake rests centred on the plate and stand with the pan removed and the assembly still.
comparisons.reason: Two-arm load sharing and flipping are materially different from seating two tools on coupled screw-and-nut hardware and preserving a calibrated setting.

comparisons.objective: Wipe an entire monitor lead and its end pieces outward in one pass, then place it on a drape.
comparisons.physical_skill: Maintain sliding contact along a deformable cord, switch hand roles, and avoid backtracking or re-wiping.
comparisons.success_condition: All cord marks and end-piece faces are wiped once, the lead lies on the drape, and forbidden reverse strokes never occur.
comparisons.reason: Deformable one-way wiping and surface coverage do not overlap the candidate's threaded stop adjustment and retention test.

comparisons.objective: Measure exactly two level scoops of formula powder into a bottle.
comparisons.physical_skill: Scoop loose powder, strike each heap against a leveling bar, and pour through a bottle neck without packing or spilling.
comparisons.success_condition: Bottle mass is within the two-scoop window, both scoops were leveled, spill is limited, and the scoop is released.
comparisons.reason: Bulk-material metering and strike-off are unrelated to coupled rotary adjustment, jam-nut locking, and repeated mechanical cycling.

comparisons.objective: Unlock a twist-lock extension pole, extend it to a mark, relock it, and verify it under a 50 N axial push.
comparisons.physical_skill: Counter-rotate two loose coaxial tubes, slide one to length while stabilizing the other, then reverse-twist the friction cam.
comparisons.success_condition: Length is within 10 mm, the cam is relocked, and the released pole shortens under 2 mm during the load test.
comparisons.reason: Both set and verify a retained mechanical adjustment, but PR-1855 tests direct tube countertwist plus axial draw; the candidate tests simultaneous driver/wrench seating and countertorque that prevents a jam nut from rotating an already-set screw.

comparisons.objective: Release a game disc from its case hub and insert it upright into a console slot.
comparisons.physical_skill: Press a release while edge-grasping a thin disc, reorient it, and perform narrow slot insertion.
comparisons.success_condition: The drive takes the correctly aligned disc; drops zero the trial and partial credit covers release or shallow insertion.
comparisons.reason: Press-to-release extraction and thin-object insertion do not test setting or locking an adjustable stop.

comparisons.objective: Choose and seat the correct lids on two serving pans while leaving a spoon in place.
comparisons.physical_skill: Handle broad thin lids and align a utensil notch over the obstructing spoon handle.
comparisons.success_condition: Both pans are fully covered with lids flat and centred, the spoon undisturbed, and hands clear for one second.
comparisons.reason: The indexed record has no task.json/spec versions, but its detailed body establishes lid selection and planar seating, clearly unlike screw/jam-nut counterholding and retained opening verification.

comparisons.objective: Secure an installed clevis pin by bending the cotter-pin legs to opposite sides.
comparisons.physical_skill: Apply localized non-prehensile force to plastically bend two small legs without rebending them.
comparisons.success_condition: Both legs remain at least 60 degrees on opposite sides, still and clear for one second; significant rebending zeros the trial.
comparisons.reason: Permanent plastic deformation of a split pin is different from reversible screw adjustment, locknut tightening, and cyclic retention testing.

comparisons.objective: Prove a voltage detector before and after testing a bar, or stop safely when proving fails.
comparisons.physical_skill: Operate buttons and maneuver a long detector stick through a safety-critical prove-test-prove procedure.
comparisons.success_condition: Working and failed-tester seeds require the correct timed indications, touches, or safe withdrawal sequence.
comparisons.reason: This primarily tests procedural electrical verification and long-tool positioning, not mechanical adjustment or countertorque locking.

comparisons.objective: Hang two wine glasses upside down in an overhead stemware rack.
comparisons.physical_skill: Grip thin stems, raise each foot above the lips, enter through the open end, slide along a channel, and release.
comparisons.success_condition: Glasses hang straight with feet resting on both lips, still and clear; knockover zeros the trial.
comparisons.reason: Channel threading and fragile-object suspension have no meaningful overlap with tool-seated stop adjustment or retained-motion testing.

comparisons.objective: Remove a named cartridge fuse from spring clips with an insulated tong puller and place it in a tray.
comparisons.physical_skill: Grip the correct fuse with a tool and rock its two ends out sequentially without disturbing neighbors.
comparisons.success_condition: The target fuse leaves both clips while held by the puller and rests in the tray; neighbor movement zeros the trial.
comparisons.reason: Tool use is shared only generically; sequential levering and extraction from clips differ from two-tool screw/nut countertorque and setting preservation.

comparisons.objective: Feed a laminating pouch sealed-edge first and square into a laminator, then release it to the rollers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Orient and feed a thin sheet precisely with correct release timing at a powered nip.
comparisons.success_condition: A square sealed-edge bite exits successfully; open-edge feeding or continued gripping after draw causes a latched jam.
comparisons.reason: Thin-sheet orientation and roller handoff do not test mechanical calibration, locking, or post-lock functional cycles.

comparisons.objective: Reconnect a sink stopper by inserting its pivot rod through a hidden internal eye and seating the pivot ball.
comparisons.physical_skill: Coordinate stopper orientation with blind rod insertion through nested bores, then release the parts.
comparisons.success_condition: External geometry and a force-based movement test confirm engagement and ball seating after a still, hands-clear dwell.
comparisons.reason: Both use post-action functional verification, but PR-1857 tests hidden coaxial insertion and linkage engagement, not preserving a screw setting against locknut torque.

comparisons.objective: Lower a bent steel tube into a checking fixture so all four legs enter their slots together.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually hold a rigid spatial tube level and achieve simultaneous multi-point alignment without catching or dropping it.
comparisons.success_condition: All four legs rest on their slot floors, the tube is released and still, and excessive drop height invalidates the result.
comparisons.reason: The record lacks indexed task.json/spec versions and a complete partial-score rubric, but its body clearly tests simultaneous fixture seating rather than adjustment, threaded locking, or cycling.

comparisons.objective: Remove a tagged bin from the middle of a gravity-flow lane without allowing the following bin to run down prematurely.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold back a gravity-driven bin while extracting and placing its neighbor, then release the lane to close up.
comparisons.success_condition: The reject rests in its tote, the next bin moved at most 2 cm before placement, and remaining bins settle against the stop.
comparisons.reason: Dynamic hold-back during bin extraction differs from rotational counterholding used to preserve a precision stop during locknut tightening.

comparisons.objective: Disassemble take-apart kitchen shears and leave both halves flat in a washing tray.
comparisons.physical_skill: Rotate two halves until a keyed pivot aligns, separate them axially, and handle only molded grips.
comparisons.success_condition: Both halves remain independently separated, supported and released; full credit requires both lying flat inside the tray.
comparisons.reason: Keyed-pivot alignment and disassembly do not test setting an adjustable limit, locking it with opposing tools, or verifying retained motion.

comparisons.objective: Wire a door lamp through a junction-box hinge, clip its cord, connect it, and latch the door; the candidate instead calibrates and locks a gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Flexible-cord routing, plug insertion, clipping, and door latching versus concentric driver/wrench seating and counter-torque locking.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires connected and clipped wiring to survive an open-close door test without pinching; candidate requires a retained 90° stop across three released actuation cycles.
comparisons.reason: Functional cycling is shared, but this record tests deformable cable management and enclosure closure, not preserving an adjustment while tightening its jam nut.

comparisons.objective: Collect three litter items with a trigger-operated reacher and place them in a bin; the candidate adjusts a robot-gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Support and aim a long tool while pulling its trigger, grasping remote objects, and transporting them versus two-tool coaxial adjustment and counterholding.
comparisons.success_condition: Credit follows items lifted or deposited without direct gripper contact; candidate follows angular accuracy, nut retention, repeated motion, and released clearance.
comparisons.reason: The shared use of two arms and a tool is generic; the tested remote grasp-and-transfer ability is unrelated to retaining a locked mechanical setting.

comparisons.objective: Seat and level a surface-roughness drive with a thumbscrew, then run its traverse; the candidate adjusts and locks a gripper opening stop before cycling it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Precision seating on a shaft and anvil followed by single-screw leveling versus simultaneous driver counterholding and thin-jam-nut tightening on one coupled adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires seated geometry, horizontal level, completed 4.790 mm traverse, and clear hands; candidate requires a retained 90° stop, locked nuts, and three repeatable cycles.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest record because both adjust a mechanism and function-test it, but it lacks the candidate's defining ability: locking an adjustable screw without disturbing its setting.

comparisons.objective: Carry a full cup to a coaster while avoiding an open laptop; the candidate services a gripper adjustment.
comparisons.physical_skill: Upright transport and obstacle clearance with spill avoidance versus seated rotary tools, counterholding, and mechanical verification.
comparisons.success_condition: Scores cup progress subject to laptop-clearance, tilt, and landing-speed safety caps; candidate scores locked angle retention and repeated gripper motion.
comparisons.reason: The tested abilities and outcomes are unrelated beyond generic careful manipulation.

comparisons.objective: Align and load four square blanks into a close-clearance gravity magazine; the candidate sets and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Repeated planar pickup, yaw alignment, and vertical insertion versus two-tool rotary adjustment and counter-torque locking.
comparisons.success_condition: Score is the number of flat, supported, still blanks inside the channel; candidate requires one precise mechanical setting to remain locked through three cycles.
comparisons.reason: Close-clearance insertion does not test adjustable-stop calibration, jam-nut locking, or retained function.

comparisons.objective: Tare an analytical balance and dose granules to 1.00 g behind its draft shield; the candidate calibrates a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Door operation, container placement, button pressing, and incremental pouring versus coaxial tool seating and coupled torque control.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires a valid empty-boat tare, target mass, closed shield, and spill control; candidate requires angular accuracy, nut retention, cyclic repeatability, and release.
comparisons.reason: No ability-level overlap exists beyond sequencing several physical operations.

comparisons.objective: Replace a worn soft gripper finger, restore its plate, and place three screws; the candidate adjusts an assembled gripper's opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Part identification, removal, replacement, plate handling, and small-part insertion versus driver/wrench counterholding on a coupled screw and jam nut.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires the worn finger binned, new finger seated, plate placed, and three screws inserted; candidate requires a locked 90° setting and retained motion over three cycles.
comparisons.reason: Both service robot grippers, but industrial labels and component proximity do not erase the different tested abilities: replacement assembly versus torque-sensitive calibration and locking.

comparisons.objective: Seat and quarter-turn a Sankey keg coupler, then lock its over-centre handle and probe; the candidate calibrates and locks an angular stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bayonet alignment and rotation followed by lever actuation while managing attached lines versus concentric screw adjustment and jam-nut counterholding.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires caught and rotated coupler, locked handle, extended probe, intact lines, and release; candidate requires a target angle retained through repeated gripper cycles.
comparisons.reason: Both create a mechanically locked state, but the keg task tests bayonet installation and lever engagement, not preserving an adjustable setting against locknut torque.

comparisons.objective: Carry a loaded hotel pan level, lower it into a close-fitting well, and release it; the candidate adjusts a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual heavy-load stabilization, spill-limited transport, and tight-fit lowering versus precision rotary adjustment and counter-torque locking.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires level, spill-free seating of the released pan; candidate requires a locked angular setting, retained nuts, three cycles, and clear tools.
comparisons.reason: The record tests coordinated load transport and seating, with no relevant adjustable fastener or retention verification.

comparisons.objective: Pipe a joined ridged shell border on a cake; the candidate calibrates and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Continuous pressure control synchronized with nozzle motion and icing deposition versus discrete coaxial driver/wrench manipulation.
comparisons.success_condition: Scores valid deposited length, shell shape, ridges, cleanliness, and released dispenser; candidate scores angle tolerance, locking, repeated return, and clearance.
comparisons.reason: No meaningful tested-ability overlap exists.

comparisons.objective: Insert a stripped conductor into a rail terminal and tighten its clamp screw; the candidate sets and jam-nut-locks a gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold a spring-return conductor seated while repeatedly driving one screw; candidate counterholds the adjustment screw with one tool while tightening a concentric nut with another.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires correct conductor insertion, clamp-down, tightness, and tool withdrawal; candidate requires preserving a 90° adjustment, both nuts retained, and three repeatable cycles.
comparisons.reason: This record shares bimanual holding and screwdriver regrasping, but explicitly has no driver reaction torque and does not test locknut-induced setting drift or post-lock cyclic retention.

comparisons.objective: Rotate a multimeter selector to its OFF detent; the candidate adjusts and locks a gripper stop before function testing.
comparisons.physical_skill: Direct finger contact on one shallow rotary control versus two seated tools applying coordinated opposing torque to a screw and jam nut.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires final selector angle and two seconds of stillness; candidate additionally requires physical locking, nut retention, three motion cycles, and hands-off clearance.
comparisons.reason: Target-angle rotation alone does not test preservation of an adjustable setpoint during mechanical locking.

comparisons.objective: Stop a spinning centrifuge, wait, open it, remove a sample tube, and rack the tube; the candidate services a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Safe-state recognition, button and lid operation, and tube extraction/insertion versus precision two-tool rotary manipulation.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires rotor stopped before opening and an upright tube in the rack; candidate requires locked angular calibration and repeatable actuation.
comparisons.reason: No meaningful physical-skill or success-condition overlap exists.

comparisons.objective: Align a long blanking panel with both U6 rack holes, push both clips home, and release it; the candidate adjusts a robot gripper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual long-part alignment and simultaneous two-peg insertion versus coaxial driver/wrench seating and torque control.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires correct rack-unit placement, both ends home, and released dwell; candidate requires a locked 90° stop retained over three cycles.
comparisons.reason: Both are relevant to AI infrastructure, but domain membership and release checks do not make rack-panel insertion equivalent to stop calibration and jam-nut locking.

comparisons.objective: Bend copper tube to 90° while compensating for hidden springback; the candidate sets a gripper's maximum opening to 90° and locks it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Iterative irreversible lever bending, relaxing, observing springback, and correcting versus reversible screw adjustment followed by counter-torque jam-nut locking.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires the relaxed tube angle within 87°–93° with the lever and hands clear; candidate requires the stop angle retained within tolerance through three articulated cycles.
comparisons.reason: The shared target angle and post-action verification are superficial; this record tests empirical springback compensation, not preserving an adjustment during locking.

comparisons.objective: Turn two eggs from lying sideways to small-end-down positions in carton cups; the candidate adjusts and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Fragile-object grasping, shape-based end recognition, reorientation, and placement versus precision rotary tool use and counter-torque.
comparisons.success_condition: The PR body specifies per-egg cup-centering, depth, orientation, rest, release, and a one-second two-egg hold; candidate requires a retained locked angle over cycles.
comparisons.reason: No task.json/spec version was available, but the complete PR body provides enough objective and scoring detail to establish a clearly unrelated tested ability.

comparisons.objective: Use a platform edge as a pivot to push a heavy carton up a step while keeping it upright; the candidate calibrates a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual load tilting, edge engagement, pushing, and balance control versus small-scale coaxial tool seating and counter-torque.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires staged or complete stable carton support on the platform without excessive tilt; candidate requires angular calibration, locked nuts, cycling, and clearance.
comparisons.reason: No meaningful mechanism or outcome overlap exists.

comparisons.objective: Choose and stack lighting gels whose combined transmission matches a reference; the candidate adjusts a gripper stop.

comparisons.success_condition: The PR body scores transmitted-colour match, extra gels, pose stability, and reference disturbance; candidate scores retained mechanical angle and cyclic function.
comparisons.reason: No task.json/spec version was available, but the detailed PR body establishes a color-combination and stacking task unrelated to torque-sensitive adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Use a physical mouse to drag a file into a specified on-screen folder; the candidate calibrates and locks a gripper stop.

comparisons.success_condition: Requires a correct digital drop, released button and mouse, and avoidance of wrong folders or mat departure; candidate requires angular retention, nuts retained, and repeated actuation.
comparisons.reason: No meaningful objective, physical mechanism, or outcome overlap exists.

comparisons.objective: Test a seat-belt retractor by slow pull, jerk-triggered locking, and rewind; candidate sets and locks a gripper opening stop, then cycles it.

comparisons.objective: Select a reach rod and press a guarded reset button through a port; candidate adjusts and locks a robot-gripper stop.

comparisons.objective: Seat a condenser on a ground-glass joint and snap a retaining clip over the joint.

comparisons.success_condition: Specified shoots severed, flowers intact, and shears returned versus locked stop angle and repeated retained motion.

comparisons.objective: Pick four conveyor parts before lane-dependent deadlines; candidate adjusts and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Timed interception and pick-and-place differ from force-controlled threaded adjustment and counterholding.
comparisons.success_condition: Cubes deposited before leaving reach versus precise angle, locking, release clearance, and three cycles.
comparisons.reason: Scheduling and moving-object manipulation do not overlap the candidate’s mechanical calibration ability.

comparisons.objective: Singulate touching parcels on a moving belt before scanning; candidate adjusts and locks a gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Dynamic parcel spacing on conveyance differs from concentric two-tool adjustment and locking.
comparisons.success_condition: Two measured inter-parcel gaps of at least 5 cm versus retained 90° opening after lock and cycling.
comparisons.reason: The objectives, physical constraints, and observable outcomes are unrelated.

comparisons.objective: Fit, orient, and slowly plunge a filled French press; candidate adjusts and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Coaxial lid insertion, vessel stabilization, and rate-limited plunging differ from two-tool screw/nut countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: Lid seated, spout closed, plunger depressed without spill or excessive speed versus stop angle locked and cycle-retained.
comparisons.reason: Both involve stabilization, but their mechanisms, hazards, and graded outcomes differ.

comparisons.objective: Release, swing, and extend a car sun visor to cover a window band; candidate adjusts and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sequential manipulation of clip, swivel, roll, and slide joints differs from concentric driver/wrench torque coordination.
comparisons.success_condition: At least 80% band coverage after release versus a precise opening limit locked without drift and cycle-verified.
comparisons.reason: Articulated motion is shared only generically; the tested abilities and end states differ.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets and locks a DRG 80 gripper opening stop at 90° and verifies retained motion; PR-2253 strikes a safety match, lights a candle, and disposes of the match safely.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests concentric two-tool screw/jam-nut adjustment, bimanual countertorque, setting preservation, tool withdrawal, and articulated-cycle verification. PR-2253 tests stabilizing a matchbox, controlled match striking, flame-to-wick placement and dwell, and safe burning-match transfer. Shared bimanual manipulation is only generic.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a locked opening within angular tolerances, retained nuts, three repeatable cycles with limited drift, and hands/tools clear. PR-2253 requires force/speed/distance-gated ignition, wick-proximity and ignition dwells, the lit candle upright, the spent match in the ashtray, the box down, and hands clear, with fire-specific zero/cap failures. Both available spec versions provide these rubric details.
comparisons.reason: The tasks test meaningfully different mechanisms and abilities: preserving a mechanical adjustment against locknut reaction and proving repeatable motion versus producing and managing ignition through a struck match. Neither objective nor its defining physical skill or terminal outcome substantially overlaps.

comparisons.objective: Pack selected boxes to match a printed two-layer plan; candidate adjusts and locks an industrial gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tight-tolerance placement and pushing of cartons differ from coaxial tool seating and reaction-bearing locking.
comparisons.success_condition: Four boxes within 5 mm face tolerances with distractors excluded versus locked angle retained through articulation.
comparisons.reason: The task tests spatial packing rather than mechanical calibration.

comparisons.objective: Hold a cord taut and cut it safely with a knife; candidate adjusts and locks a gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tensioning a deformable cord while applying a blade differs from preserving a threaded setting under jam-nut torque.
comparisons.success_condition: Cord severed away from hand and anchor, knife safely released versus locked stop angle and successful repeated cycles.
comparisons.reason: Bimanual reaction control is generic; cutting and threaded adjustment are different tested abilities.

comparisons.objective: Free a tote strap caught on a rake and lower the loaded tote safely; candidate calibrates and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Entanglement detection and deformable-strap freeing differ from two-tool threaded adjustment and countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: Tote on table with contents retained and rake on shelf versus precise stop setting retained after locking and cycles.
comparisons.reason: No mechanism or outcome overlap beyond general bimanual manipulation.

comparisons.objective: Lift and tip a wide box into a narrow slot on edge; candidate adjusts and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual compression grasp and edge-assisted reorientation differ from driver/wrench seating and torque regulation.
comparisons.success_condition: Box upright in slot versus jam-nut seated, 90° setting retained, and three successful actuations.
comparisons.reason: The task tests large-object reorientation, not mechanical setting retention.

comparisons.objective: Tension and pluck a chalk line to make a straight mark; candidate adjusts and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Maintaining line tension while lifting and releasing its midpoint differs from concentric countertorque on screw and nut.
comparisons.success_condition: Single straight print through the marks and reel returned versus locked angular stop retained through cycles.
comparisons.reason: Shared bimanual tension management is generic and serves different tested abilities.

comparisons.objective: Declutch a powered valve actuator and manually close it; candidate adjusts and locks a gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Holding a lever while turning a handwheel until clutch engagement differs from seating separate coaxial tools and counterholding an adjusted screw during jam-nut tightening.
comparisons.success_condition: Clutch engaged and valve closed versus precise stop angle locked without drift and verified through three released cycles.
comparisons.reason: This is a plausible primitive-level neighbor, but its mode-change-and-turn ability is meaningfully different; no indexed task.json/spec exists, and the PR body omits full setup dimensions without creating ambiguity about that distinction.

comparisons.objective: Fit an end bracket to a loose DIN rail and tighten its clamp screw; candidate adjusts and locks a gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bracing a rail while mounting a bracket and driving one screw differs from using a driver and wrench on coupled screw/nut hardware to preserve a calibrated setting.
comparisons.success_condition: Bracket seated flush and tightened to 0.5 Nm with rail motion limited versus 90° stop retained within tolerance through three cycles.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest general assembly/tool-use record, but it lacks the candidate’s essential set-then-lock countertorque and functional-retention test.

comparisons.objective: Undo a tight bolt using a ratchet initially set to tighten, then return the ratchet; candidate instead sets and locks a gripper opening stop and verifies cycling.
comparisons.physical_skill: Selector flipping, socket seating, and repeated ratchet strokes versus simultaneous hex-driver counterholding and jam-nut tightening on a coupled adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: Bolt backed out at least one turn and ratchet returned; over-tightening beyond 20° fails. Exact partial tiers are absent. Candidate requires retained 90° opening, locked nuts, three cycles, and released clearance.
comparisons.reason: Both use rotary tools, but the record tests tool-mode recognition and one-way ratcheting, not preserving a screw setting while locking its concentric jam nut.

comparisons.objective: Set a telescoping luggage handle to a marked working length and leave its spring pin locked; candidate calibrates and locks a gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Unlocking and translating telescoping rails until a pin re-engages versus coaxial driver/wrench seating and countertorque during jam-nut locking.
comparisons.success_condition: Usable marked length, pin engagement, hands withdrawn, and a two-second hold; exact length tolerance and score tiers are absent. Candidate additionally requires repeated retained actuation.
comparisons.reason: The shared adjust-and-lock abstraction is generic; indexed linear translation with a spring pin tests a different ability from coupled threaded adjustment and counterholding.

comparisons.objective: Abrasively score an ampoule neck, break it open, retain the cap, and return the opener; candidate adjusts a gripper stop without fracture.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual stabilization, circumferential abrasive motion, controlled breakage, and fragment retention versus two-tool threaded countertorque and cycle testing.
comparisons.success_condition: At least 34 of 36 neck sectors must qualify before break, with the cap retained; unscored break is rejected. The complete partial-credit ladder is absent.
comparisons.reason: Controlled abrasion and fracture are meaningfully different from setting, jam-nut locking, and verifying an articulated stop.

comparisons.objective: Mount a phone in a sprung car holder so its arms grip the phone; candidate sets and locks the maximum opening of an industrial gripper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Across versions, either cock-and-trigger or continuously hold open paired clamp arms while positioning a phone; candidate uses concentric tools and countertorque on threaded hardware.
comparisons.success_condition: Phone seated and edge-clamped, released and still for one second, with drop and face-clamping failures; candidate requires angle tolerance, nut retention, three cycles, and clearance.
comparisons.reason: Manipulating a spring clamp around an inserted phone does not test preserving an adjustable screw position while tightening its jam nut.

comparisons.objective: Place a swing-top stopper and snap its wire bail over centre to seal a bottle; candidate configures a gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold a free bottle, guide a linked stopper, and actuate an over-centre linkage versus driver/wrench seating, countertorque, and stop adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: Stopper aligned, lever past centre with stretched link, bottle upright, hands released, and full state stable for one second; candidate instead verifies retained opening through three cycles.
comparisons.reason: The record tests linked stopper placement and over-centre closure mechanics, not coupled screw-and-locknut calibration.

comparisons.objective: Install a 2.5-inch SSD in a tool-less carrier; candidate sets and locks the gripper's opening limit.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold a sprung rail open while aligning a thin drive and four side holes with pins, then release the rail; candidate counterholds a screw while tightening a nut with separate tools.
comparisons.success_condition: All four pins engaged, rail closed, drive flat and correctly oriented, stable for one second; earlier versions also penalize falls or wrong orientation.
comparisons.reason: Spring-rail retention and multi-pin insertion test constrained assembly alignment, not coupled threaded calibration or retained functional cycling.

comparisons.objective: Unlock, remove, and lay down a wheelchair armrest; candidate adjusts a robot gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold a spring release while lifting two long posts squarely from sockets and controlling a 1.2 kg assembly versus two-tool countertorque and articulated verification.
comparisons.success_condition: Both posts clear, armrest moved outward and laid safely on its side; dropping fails, with partial credit for release and extraction progress.
comparisons.reason: Simultaneous latch release and parallel extraction are materially different from preserving a threaded angular adjustment while locking it.

comparisons.objective: Remove an obstruction and insert a knife into a holder; candidate adjusts and locks a gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Safe obstacle removal followed by narrow-slot knife insertion versus coupled screw/nut tool manipulation and torque regulation.
comparisons.success_condition: Knife inserted to specified depth and pose, with full credit only if the toy is safely released outside the holder; invalid or fallen states fail.
comparisons.reason: Clearing an insertion path and storing a blade tests obstacle handling and alignment, not angular calibration or jam-nut retention.

comparisons.objective: Fit a funnel and pour beads into a narrow-neck bottle; candidate sets and locks gripper geometry.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tool selection, funnel insertion, jug handling, and granular pouring versus hex-driver/wrench counterholding and articulated testing.
comparisons.success_condition: Credit follows delivered bead count, with full score for at least 22 of 24 settled beads; candidate scores retained angular setting and lock integrity.
comparisons.reason: Granular transfer through a selected funnel is a different tested ability from coupled threaded adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Retrofit a split cable guide at a panel and verify service-drawer travel; candidate calibrates a gripper stop and verifies jaw motion.
comparisons.physical_skill: Fit a split guide around a connected cable, close a keeper, preserve plugs, and trigger drawer travel versus counterhold a stop screw while tightening its jam nut.
comparisons.success_condition: Guide locked before release, drawer travels at least 48 mm, sleeve clears, plugs remain seated, and proof holds two seconds; loss conditions permanently fail.
comparisons.reason: Both include hands-off functional verification, but guide installation and cable-clearance proof do not test preservation of a threaded angular setting under locknut torque.

comparisons.objective: Empty a robot-vacuum dustbin into a waste box, reseat it, and close its doors; candidate adjusts a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold a bin while pressing a door release, control granular discharge, and replace the bin versus precision two-tool threaded adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: At least nine dust balls captured, bin reseated with doors shut, and arms returned; partial credit follows delivered quantity.
comparisons.reason: Triggered dumping and reseating a container are unrelated to coupled screw/jam-nut calibration and retained cycling.

comparisons.objective: Install a booster-seat tray at its second ratchet notch; candidate sets a gripper to a target opening angle and locks it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Align a wide tray on two rails and advance two sprung catches into matching notches versus coaxial driver/wrench countertorque on one adjustable stop.
comparisons.success_condition: Both catches locked at notch two, tray released and still for one second; wrong notches earn partial credit and movement or falls fail.
comparisons.reason: Although both choose and retain a setting, dual-rail insertion with paired ratchet catches tests a different physical ability from threaded setting preservation.

comparisons.objective: Remove an old toner cartridge, insert a new one on printer guide rails, and close the door; candidate configures a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Handle large cartridges through keyed rails and notches while avoiding a roller versus fine two-tool countertorque and angular adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: Old cartridge safely placed, new cartridge seated, door shut, hands clear, and state stable for one second; printer movement, roller contact, or drops fail.
comparisons.reason: Guided consumable extraction and insertion do not overlap meaningfully with jam-nut locking or repeated stop verification.

comparisons.objective: Counterhold a loose soap bottle while rotating its captive pump head until it springs up; candidate sets and locks an industrial gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual relative rotation of bottle and pump to clear retaining shoulders versus simultaneous hex-driver counterholding and wrench tightening on screw and nut.
comparisons.success_condition: Pump head rises at least 15 mm relative to an upright bottle, hands clear, and state stable for 21 samples; candidate requires a retained target angle and three actuation cycles.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest generic counterholding match, but releasing a spring-loaded packaging latch does not test preserving a screw setting while locking a jam nut.

comparisons.objective: Clamp a hanging folder around a packet and hook all four rod ends onto frame rails; candidate configures a gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually pinch an articulated folder, retain loose contents, and align four suspension points versus threaded tool use and torque coordination.
comparisons.success_condition: All four hooks seated, folder suspended, packet retained upright, hands at least 80 mm clear, and state stable for one second.
comparisons.reason: Suspended multi-point placement with content retention is materially different from stop adjustment and locknut verification.

comparisons.objective: Clear a towel from a rice-cooker steam vent before pressing COOK; candidate adjusts and locks gripper hardware.
comparisons.physical_skill: Recognize and remove a safety obstruction, place it securely, and actuate a plunger versus coordinated tool seating and countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: Vent clear before activation, towel supported, button released, grippers withdrawn, and final state held one second; unsafe activation permanently fails.
comparisons.reason: Safe prerequisite handling and button activation do not test mechanical calibration, locknut retention, or repeated actuation.

comparisons.objective: Identify hidden cable-to-device correspondences and place the correct two plugs in holders; candidate calibrates a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Interactive perception through cable tugging, deformable tracing, and selective plug placement versus threaded two-tool manipulation.
comparisons.success_condition: Red and blue plugs released in matching holders while other plugs remain near their starts; wrong placement or excessive disturbance fails.
comparisons.reason: The record's core ability is causal cable tracing under occlusion, not mechanical adjustment or torque-controlled locking.

comparisons.objective: Simultaneously release two lid latches, lift the lid, and place it beside the case; candidate adjusts and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Coordinated bilateral latch retraction and lifting of the same panel versus counterholding one threaded setting while another tool tightens its nut.
comparisons.success_condition: Full score for the lid removed and resting flat beside the case; partial credit for one or both latches and lift progress.
comparisons.reason: Simultaneous latch release and panel extraction are different from coupled screw/jam-nut torque control.

comparisons.objective: Fill and truthfully tick only the three tubes supportable by the limited sample; candidate configures industrial gripper mechanics.
comparisons.physical_skill: Pipette operation, liquid allocation, and physical record marking versus coaxial tool seating, wrenching, and articulated verification.
comparisons.success_condition: Three tubes filled and ticked, fourth empty and unticked; water use or false ticks score zero, with detailed progress tiers.
comparisons.reason: Liquid handling and honest record-state management have no meaningful physical overlap with gripper stop locking.

comparisons.objective: Hold a printed part at a marked height while closing a bench vise; candidate sets and locks a gripper's own opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: One hand positions a loose workpiece while the other rotates a vise knob; candidate seats two tools concentrically and counterholds the adjustment screw against jam-nut torque.
comparisons.success_condition: Part clamped with at least 5 N, upright, and its line within 2 mm of jaw tops; candidate requires retained 90° opening, nut retention, release, and three cycles.
comparisons.reason: Both combine holding with tightening, but vise workpiece placement lacks the candidate's coupled screw/nut setting-preservation and post-lock functional-retention test.

comparisons.objective: Read a diagnostic blink code, replace the indicated module, and verify a green status; candidate adjusts and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Temporal signal interpretation, keyed module extraction/insertion, and button holding versus fine two-tool countertorque on threaded hardware.
comparisons.success_condition: Failed module removed, teal spare seated in socket 3, healthy modules retained, DIAG held for green verification, and released state stable one second.
comparisons.reason: Diagnostic selection and keyed field-replaceable-unit swapping test a different ability; generic post-work verification does not create overlap.

comparisons.objective: Unfold, orient, and hang folding headphones; candidate calibrates and locks a gripper opening stop, then verifies retained motion.
comparisons.physical_skill: Headphone handling uses passive-joint articulation and elastic-object placement, not coaxial driver seating, wrench countertorque, or locknut setting retention.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires unfolded/swiveled joints and stable hanging for 5 s; candidate requires a 90° opening, seated/retained nuts, three repeat cycles, limited drift, and tool clearance.
comparisons.reason: The tested abilities and final functional outcomes are meaningfully different despite both manipulating articulated mechanisms.

comparisons.objective: Extend a spring-return tape and mark a board at 300 mm; candidate adjusts and locks a gripper stop at 90°.
comparisons.physical_skill: Requires resisting tape retraction while placing a pen mark, not coaxial screw driving with a thin-nut wrench and countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: Checks mark position, tape extension, and pen release; candidate checks stop angle, locking hardware, repeated actuation, drift, and tool withdrawal.
comparisons.reason: Although both preserve a setting against a restoring force, the record tests simultaneous measuring and marking rather than mechanical lock-setting retention.

comparisons.objective: Open a push-and-turn child-resistant bottle cap; candidate calibrates and locks an adjustable gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both combine rotation with constraint and may use bimanual stabilization, but the cap requires axial pressing and unscrewing rather than driver/wrench countertorque on coupled screw-and-nut hardware.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires cap removal or loosening without tipping or spilling; candidate requires a retained 90° stop through three close-open cycles with limited drift and both nuts retained.
comparisons.reason: The record tests release of an interlocked closure, while the candidate tests precise adjustment preservation during locking and subsequent functional cycling.

comparisons.objective: Assemble four cylindrical cells between holder halves in a jig; candidate adjusts and locks an already-assembled gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Requires repeated polarity-aware close-clearance insertion and final holder alignment, rather than coupled screw/nut adjustment with reaction counterholding.
comparisons.success_condition: Checks holder placement, two/four seated cells, top-holder alignment, release, and loss; candidate checks 90° accuracy, locking, retained cycling, drift, and tool clearance.
comparisons.reason: Both concern robot-related assembly, but cell insertion and stack assembly do not test preserving a calibrated stop during locknut tightening.

comparisons.objective: Rotate a free countertop display and insert two cartons into its empty rear pockets; candidate adjusts and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Requires stabilizing a freely rotating rack during close-fitting box placement, not tool seating or coupled screw-and-locknut countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: Checks display orientation, one/two seated boxes, stability, and tip avoidance; candidate checks angular calibration, hardware retention, cycle repeatability, drift, and release clearance.
comparisons.reason: The record tests placement into moving pockets, whereas the candidate tests secured adjustment and retained mechanism function.

comparisons.objective: Open a cabinet, hang two assigned key rings on hooks, seat the blades in guides, and close the door; candidate sets and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Requires small-ring threading, guide insertion, object release, and door articulation, rather than driver/wrench counterholding.
comparisons.success_condition: Checks assigned hook capture, millimetric final key poses, low contact, and closed released door over 20 controls; candidate checks opening angle, retained hardware, repeated cycling, drift, and clearance.
comparisons.reason: Precision key hanging and cabinet closure do not test adjustment retention under locknut torque.

comparisons.objective: Back-butter a replacement tile, invert it, place it in a gap, and bed it level; candidate calibrates a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Requires trowel coverage, stabilizing and reorienting a tile, close placement, and pressing; candidate requires coaxial driver/wrench engagement and countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: Scores adhesive coverage, placement, squareness, lippage, bedding, tool release, and clearance; candidate scores angle, nut retention, repeated motion, drift, and clearance.
comparisons.reason: Tool use is shared only generically; adhesive application and tile bedding test a different manipulation outcome.

comparisons.objective: Remove a fragile egg obstruction before placing a pot on a trivet; candidate adjusts and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Requires hazard inspection, gentle egg relocation, and stable pot placement rather than threaded adjustment with two tools.
comparisons.success_condition: Checks egg clearance and safe support, pot support, release, stillness, and strict contact-damage limits; candidate checks angle accuracy, nuts, functional cycles, drift, and clearance.
comparisons.reason: The record tests safe obstruction clearing and placement, with no calibrated mechanism or lock-retention ability.

comparisons.objective: Lift and reposition a tethered lamp so its plug can reach a tray; candidate calibrates and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Requires reasoning about tether reach, safe appliance lifting, and cord/plug placement, not coaxial tool seating or countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: Checks safe non-dragged lamp relocation, plug delivery, uprightness, release, and tether integrity; candidate checks 90° setting, nut retention, cycles, drift, and clearance.
comparisons.reason: Tether-aware relocation is meaningfully different from preserving a threaded stop setting during locking.

comparisons.objective: Pull a cable from a feed channel to a 30 cm length mark and release it straight; candidate sets and locks a gripper opening angle.
comparisons.physical_skill: Requires cable extraction, handover, visual length regulation, and flexible-object control, rather than driver/wrench countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: Checks final length tolerance, straightness, retained feed length, overshoot, release, and fixture integrity; candidate checks angular accuracy, nuts, repeated actuation, drift, and clearance.
comparisons.reason: Both regulate a target value, but cable-length positioning without locking or functional cycling tests a different physical ability.

comparisons.objective: Move three fruits from a shared bin while another arm removes utensils; candidate calibrates and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Requires collision-aware pick-and-place around an independently moving coworker, not precision tool engagement or mechanical counterholding.
comparisons.success_condition: Scores fruit placement and invalidates arm contact or utensil loss; candidate scores stop angle, hardware retention, repeated cycles, drift, and tool clearance.
comparisons.reason: The record tests dynamic shared-workspace avoidance during transport, not adjustment and lock retention.

comparisons.objective: Steady a loaf and saw off a slice of specified thickness while keeping the holding hand clear; candidate adjusts and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Requires guarded bimanual sawing and workpiece stabilization, rather than coaxial screw adjustment with wrench countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: Checks cut depth or completed slice thickness and continuous blade clearance; candidate checks angle tolerance, nut retention, repeated motion, drift, and released tools.
comparisons.reason: Bimanual stabilization is generic; cutting with a guarded blade does not test preserving an adjustable setting against tightening reaction.

comparisons.objective: After cooling, transfer a finished print plate level and install a clean plate on a printer; candidate calibrates and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Requires timing, level bimanual plate transport, loose-part retention, and locating-pin alignment rather than small-tool countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: Checks cooling order, print retention, used-plate placement, clean-plate fit, release, and stillness; candidate checks angle, nuts, three cycles, drift, and clearance.
comparisons.reason: Printer plate exchange tests transport and installation, not mechanical calibration or locknut-secured retention.

comparisons.objective: Fit a linear-guide carriage onto a rail, push it past a spring plunger to an end stop, and release; candidate adjusts and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Requires undercut rail alignment, constrained insertion, and overcoming a detent, not two-tool screw/nut countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: Checks rail capture, alignment, passage beyond the plunger, end-stop contact, release, and stillness; candidate checks calibrated angle, both nuts, repeated cycles, drift, and clearance.
comparisons.reason: Both concern robot hardware and retained mechanisms, but rail insertion past a detent does not test preserving an adjustable setting while locking it.

comparisons.objective: Push two reject cartons off a moving line while leaving good cartons undisturbed; candidate calibrates and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Requires timed lateral pushing of moving objects and selective disturbance avoidance, rather than seated-tool torque coordination.
comparisons.success_condition: Scores each correctly routed reject and penalizes disturbed good cartons or invalid routes; candidate scores angle, nut retention, functional cycles, drift, and clearance.
comparisons.reason: Dynamic sorting on a conveyor tests interception and selective pushing, not threaded adjustment retention.

comparisons.objective: Crack an egg, pull the shell apart, deposit contents in a bowl, and discard both shell halves; candidate adjusts and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Requires controlled impact, fracture-triggered bimanual separation, liquid/solid containment, and waste placement, not driver/wrench countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: Checks crack/open events, yolk and white capture, shell disposal, arm return, and stability; candidate checks angle, retained nuts, cycles, drift, and clearance.
comparisons.reason: The record tests controlled breaking and containment, which is unrelated to mechanical stop calibration.

comparisons.objective: Pour mixed coins from a jar and sort pennies and quarters into separate frames; candidate calibrates and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Requires controlled pouring and planar separation/pushing of thin loose objects, not coaxial adjustment or reaction counterholding.
comparisons.success_condition: Awards per-coin credit for correct final containment; candidate requires a precise locked angle, retained hardware, repeated actuation, bounded drift, and tool clearance.
comparisons.reason: Granular sorting and planar pushing do not exercise the candidate's coupled screw-and-locknut retention ability.

comparisons.objective: Rotate four bottles by an eighth turn while they remain seated in a pupitre; candidate sets and locks a gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both regulate angular motion and release, but bottle riddling uses direct frictional rotation about a slanted axis without tools, countertorque, or a locking fastener.
comparisons.success_condition: Body-only evidence scores each bottle turned 30–60° while still seated and released, with total failure for extraction; candidate requires a 90° stop, retained nuts, three functional cycles, and bounded drift.
comparisons.reason: No task.json/spec version is available, but the complete PR body sufficiently shows direct bottle rotation rather than calibrated threaded setting and lock retention.

comparisons.objective: Lift and swing a tonearm, then lower its stylus into the gap before track three; candidate calibrates and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Requires delicate finger-lift manipulation along a hinged arc and low-speed stylus placement, not coaxial driver/wrench countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: Body-only evidence checks correct radial gap, released stillness, touchdown-speed and slide limits; candidate checks angle, nuts, repeated cycles, drift, and tool clearance.
comparisons.reason: No task.json/spec version is available, but the complete PR body establishes precision cueing as a different tested ability from adjustment locking.

comparisons.objective: Set and lock a gripper opening stop versus lifting, aligning, inserting, and latching a laptop onto a dock.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires concentric driver-and-wrench countertorque; the dock task requires level bimanual transport, connector alignment, and bilateral pressing.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a retained 90° stop over three cycles with nuts retained and tools clear; the dock requires connector seating and both spring latches engaged without dropping or undocking.
comparisons.reason: The complete body lacks a task.json rubric but clearly tests large-object docking and bilateral latch engagement, not preservation of an adjustable setting during locknut tightening.

comparisons.objective: Set and lock a gripper stop versus replace a soap refill, close its cover, and test the pump.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses coupled coaxial tools and countertorque; the refill task uses removal, hidden keyhole insertion, sliding into a yoke, cover closure, and push testing.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a retained 90° stop over three cycles; the refill task requires the spent bottle binned, new bottle seated, cover shut, and pump stroke demonstrated.
comparisons.reason: Both end with functional testing, but the manipulated mechanisms and tested abilities—adjustment retention versus refill insertion and pump engagement—are meaningfully different.

comparisons.objective: Set and lock a rigid gripper mechanism versus cut six stitches while preserving flexible fabric.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires two-tool countertorque and articulated verification; the seam task requires precise blade placement and selective cutting without fabric damage.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades angle, locking, nut retention, cycles, and clearance; the seam task counts visibly separated stitches and invalidates all credit for cuts or tears.
