comparisons.reason: Selective cutting of deformable material is unrelated to screw-and-jam-nut adjustment and retained mechanical calibration.

comparisons.objective: Set and lock a gripper opening stop versus uncover clean ice, scoop it, and deliver it hygienically.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires coaxial tool seating and counterholding; the ice task requires lid removal, scoop loading, granular transport, source selection, and contamination avoidance.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires retained angle across three cycles; the ice task requires at least one clean-source cube settled in the bowl with scoop use and no contamination.
comparisons.reason: Tool use and release are shared only at a generic level; the board task tests hygienic source-dependent scooping rather than adjustment locking.

comparisons.objective: Set and lock an angular stop versus align a carriage with a T-rail and slide it through a detent.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires driver-and-wrench countertorque; the rail task requires close-profile insertion, square sliding, and overcoming a spring plunger.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a locked 90° setting retained through cycles; the rail task requires carriage position past the plunger against an end stop while the rail remains unmoved.
comparisons.reason: Both concern robot hardware, but profile insertion through a detent does not test maintaining a calibrated screw setting during jam-nut locking.

comparisons.objective: Set and lock a gripper stop versus sort six bottles between crowded rack levels without disturbing them.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses fine coupled-tool manipulation; the rack task uses repeated grasping, constrained horizontal placement, staging, and collision avoidance.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades retained angle and function; the rack task grades all bottles on color-matched shelves with upright stability and irreversible fall or tilt failures.
comparisons.reason: Crowded multi-object sorting and safe placement test a different ability from mechanical adjustment and countertorque locking.

comparisons.objective: Set and lock a mechanical opening stop versus configure a control panel from a setup sheet and start it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires tool seating and mechanical countertorque; the busybox requires reading settings, operating switches, dial and sliders, then simultaneous two-button pressing.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires retained stop motion; the busybox requires the P2 control state and a valid two-hand start without forbidden controls.
comparisons.reason: The busybox tests instruction-conditioned control operation and start interlocking, not mechanical calibration or resistance to locknut-induced drift.

comparisons.objective: Set and lock a gripper stop versus move a pot off a burner and switch the burner off.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses precise two-tool rotational coordination; the stove task uses pick-and-place plus slider operation.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades angle retention and repeated function; the stove task grades pot location, switch-off state, and pot safety.
comparisons.reason: No adjustment, locking, counterholding, or retained articulated setting is tested by the stove task.

comparisons.objective: Set and lock a gripper stop versus stack a block while another robot works in the shared space.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires bimanual coaxial tool use; the tower task requires timed pick-and-place and inter-robot collision avoidance.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires retained angle over cycles; the tower task requires the green block resting on the tower with no arm contact.
comparisons.reason: Shared use of two arms is superficial; the tower task tests coordination with another agent rather than adjustment locking.

comparisons.objective: Set and lock a gripper stop versus clear, open, load, and close a sliding-lid glasses box safely.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires screw-and-nut countertorque; the box task requires sequential pushing and delicate object placement around obstacles.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades retained calibration and cycling; the box task grades keys in a dish, upright glasses in the box, closed lid, and absence of listed safety violations.
comparisons.reason: Fragile-object storage and sliding-lid sequencing do not test preservation of an adjustable mechanical setting.

comparisons.objective: Set and lock a gripper stop versus insert a cotter pin and permanently bend both legs to secure a clevis.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses reversible coupled-thread countertorque with two tools; the cotter task uses insertion followed by plastic bending from opposite sides.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a locked angle retained through motion; the cotter task requires seating, two bends of at least 45°, release, and no excessive rebending.
comparisons.reason: Both secure hardware, but plastic deformation after pin insertion is a different tested ability from holding a threaded adjustment against locknut torque.

comparisons.objective: Set and lock a gripper stop versus transport a threaded collar along a curved protected guide.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses tool engagement and countertorque; the collar task requires occlusion-aware constrained transport while maintaining hidden clearance.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires retained angle and cycles; the collar task requires threading preserved, no prohibited contact, target support and alignment, release, and stillness.
comparisons.reason: The complete body lacks a task.json rubric but clearly tests protected-guide transport under changing occlusion, not adjustment locking.

comparisons.objective: Set and lock a gripper stop versus draw a measured liquid dose from a vial and return the syringe.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both are bimanual, but the candidate counterholds threaded hardware while the syringe task stabilizes a barrel during needle insertion and plunger withdrawal.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades angle retention and cycling; the syringe task requires 9–11 ml liquid, at most 1 ml air, needle removal, rack placement, release, and arm return.
comparisons.reason: Bimanual stabilization is generic; dosing through coordinated insertion and linear aspiration is meaningfully different from countertorque locking.

comparisons.objective: Set and lock a gripper stop versus orient and fit two bevelled steel coupons to a specified weld root gap.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses concentric rotary tools; weld fit-up uses reorientation and millimetre-scale planar alignment of two loose parts.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a retained angular stop over cycles; weld fit-up requires facing bevels, 1.6–3.2 mm openings at both ends, aligned ends, flatness, and stillness.
comparisons.reason: Both involve numerical setup, but weld coupon alignment does not involve locking a setting or resisting tightening reaction.

comparisons.objective: Set and lock a gripper stop versus insert the final motor magnet while preventing its neighbor from jumping out.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both require simultaneous stabilization, but the candidate applies rotational countertorque with two tools while the magnet task holds one part down during force-coupled insertion.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a locked stop retained through three cycles; the magnet task requires the correct magnet flush, no neighbor jump, and optionally arms returned.
comparisons.reason: Holding a neighboring magnet against attraction during insertion is a different ability from preserving a screw setting during jam-nut tightening.

comparisons.objective: Set and lock a gripper stop versus crossfade two audio faders without dead air or excessive overlap.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires coaxial tool seating and torque balance; the radio task requires synchronized opposite linear motion or staged one-hand motion.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades a retained mechanical setting; the radio task requires one fader closed and the other at its mark while respecting irreversible trajectory bounds.
comparisons.reason: The body provides no task.json but fully states its binary rubric; coordinated fader trajectories do not test mechanical locking or functional retention.

comparisons.objective: Set and lock a gripper stop versus squeeze spring tongs shut, engage their pull-tab lock, and store them.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both involve holding a mechanism while engaging a lock, but the candidate requires seated driver-and-wrench countertorque and possible wrench regrasping; the tongs require compression plus linear tab pulling.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a precise angle retained through repeated actuation; the tongs task requires shut arms, tab engagement, release, and placement inside a tray compartment.
comparisons.reason: The shared hold-while-locking primitive is generic; concentric torque-preserving calibration and post-lock cycle verification constitute a different tested ability from spring-tong closure.

comparisons.objective: Set and lock a gripper stop versus lift a recessed can tab to break a scored-panel seal.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires two-tool countertorque; the can task requires small-feature pinching, lever motion, and breakaway-force control.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades angle retention and repeated operation; the can task grades maximum tab lift, panel opening, hand clearance, and a one-second hold.
comparisons.reason: Levering a breakaway seal is unrelated to maintaining and locking an adjustable stop.

comparisons.objective: Set and lock a gripper stop versus rotate a window sash upright while retracting two spring latches until they engage.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses independent tools on concentric threaded parts; the window task uses bilateral latch depression while lifting a large hinged sash evenly.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires retained stop angle across cycles; the window task requires pivot retention, near-upright alignment, both latch bolts extended into slots, and stillness.
comparisons.reason: Both finish with a retained articulated state, but bilateral latch management during a large-object lift tests a meaningfully different physical ability.

comparisons.objective: Set and lock a gripper opening stop versus seat a switch line card by closing two ejector levers together.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires coaxial driver-and-wrench countertorque; the line-card task requires synchronized bilateral levering against connector resistance while avoiding card cocking.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires retained angular calibration through cycles; the card task requires both end gaps within 1 mm, both levers latched, release, and no damaging end-gap mismatch.
comparisons.reason: Synchronized connector seating and latch closure differ from preserving an adjustable threaded setting, despite both being bimanual robot-hardware service tasks.

comparisons.objective: Set and lock a gripper stop versus insert two cable connectors and route their shared slack into a guide.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses rigid two-tool rotational coordination; the cable task uses precision connector insertion and flexible-chain routing without pulling seated plugs loose.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires angle retention across motion cycles; the cable task requires both plugs released and seated for 20 controls plus the collar released in the guide.
comparisons.reason: Retention after cable routing concerns insertion and tension management, not locknut countertorque or calibrated stop adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Set and lock a gripper stop versus choose a scoop and transfer multiple loose beads into a bowl.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires fine coaxial tool use and torque balance; the bead task requires tool selection, scoop loading against a tray wall, transport, and pouring.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires retained angle over repeated cycles; the bead task counts settled delivered beads, with five or more required for full credit.
comparisons.reason: Granular scooping and tool selection share no specific adjustment, locking, or articulated-retention ability with the candidate.

comparisons.objective: Hang a deformable cable across two hooks with specified sag; candidate adjusts and locks a gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Cable shape/slack control and hook placement versus coaxial driver seating, jam-nut wrenching, and countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: Cable released in both cradles with 4–6 cm sag versus retained 90° stop after three articulated cycles and tool clearance.
comparisons.reason: The tested abilities, manipulated mechanisms, and outcomes are meaningfully different.

comparisons.objective: Route a rope in a figure-eight around twin posts; candidate sets and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Topological deformable-line winding versus coupled screw-and-locknut adjustment with bimanual counterholding.
comparisons.success_condition: Required alternating post crossings while released versus locked angular accuracy, low drift, repeated motion, and released clearance.
comparisons.reason: Shared bimanual handling is generic; neither the mechanism nor the retained outcome overlaps.

comparisons.objective: Sort cubes while yielding both arms to a person's hand; candidate performs gripper stop adjustment and locking.
comparisons.physical_skill: Human-aware shared-space avoidance plus pick-and-place versus two-tool coupled screw/nut manipulation.
comparisons.success_condition: No hand-distance/bin intrusion violation and cubes on matching mats versus retained angle, nuts, cycles, and tool clearance.
comparisons.reason: No task.json/spec version was available, so detailed setup rubric is missing; the complete body still establishes a clearly unrelated safety ability.

comparisons.objective: Recycle scrap paper while leaving a private letter untouched; candidate locks a mechanical opening adjustment.
comparisons.physical_skill: Semantic object selection and simple pick-and-place versus force-coupled driver/wrench use and functional verification.
comparisons.success_condition: Scrap in bin without moving the letter versus accurate locked opening retained over repeated actuation.
comparisons.reason: The recycling task's difficulty is selection, not threaded adjustment or setting preservation.

comparisons.objective: Push an umbrella runner until its spring latch engages, then lift the umbrella; candidate locks a gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Stabilize a handle while translating a sleeve against a spring versus coaxial rotary adjustment and jam-nut counterholding.
comparisons.success_condition: Runner latched, released, and umbrella lifted versus angle retained after locknut tightening and repeated gripper cycles.
comparisons.reason: Generic bimanual stabilization and post-action verification do not make the latch task an adjustment-lock duplicate.

comparisons.objective: Advance a sheath over a guidewire without losing the wire, then withdraw it; candidate sets a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold a deformable wire against sheath drag and perform constrained sliding versus coupled rotary screw/nut tool use.
comparisons.success_condition: Sheath seated, wire not displaced prematurely, then withdrawn and released versus locked angle retained through cycles.
comparisons.reason: The constraint-preservation theme is shared, but the actual physical ability is axial wire/sheath management rather than countertorque locking.

comparisons.objective: Tilt a tall canister through restricted shelf clearance and stand it upright; candidate locks an angular stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Constrained reorientation and placement versus coaxial rotary tool use and coupled torque control.
comparisons.success_condition: Canister released upright behind the fence versus gripper stop locked near 90° and stable over cycles.
comparisons.reason: No meaningful overlap exists beyond ordinary grasping and release.

comparisons.objective: Twist an ice tray with opposing torques, then invert it to release cubes; candidate locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual deformation through opposite end torques and controlled dumping versus concentric screw/nut countertorque and tool withdrawal.
comparisons.success_condition: Cubes freed and deposited with tray restored versus angular setting retained after tightening and repeated actuation.
comparisons.reason: Opposing torque is shared, but one tests tray flexure and release while the other tests locknut-induced setting preservation.

comparisons.objective: Knock an espresso puck from a portafilter and return the tool; candidate adjusts a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Controlled impact and momentum transfer versus precision rotary adjustment, jam-nut tightening, and counterholding.
comparisons.success_condition: Puck in knock box and portafilter released on holder versus retained angle, nuts, repeated cycles, and clearance.
comparisons.reason: Impact-based ejection is unrelated to coupled threaded locking.

comparisons.objective: Locate a DC earth fault by sectionalizing fuse circuits; candidate mechanically adjusts and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sequential fuse extraction/reinsertion guided by a meter versus coordinated driver-and-wrench countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: Faulty feeder isolated without simultaneously opening healthy circuits versus retained 90° setting after repeated cycles.
comparisons.reason: No task.json/spec version was available, so exact setup dimensions are missing; the complete body establishes a clearly unrelated diagnostic manipulation.

comparisons.objective: Erect four hinged crate walls and engage all corner catches; candidate locks a gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Swing large panels, brace the crate, and push hooks through spring catches versus concentric fine-tool rotation and countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: Four corners latched with walls upright and crate released versus locked angle retained through articulated test cycles.
comparisons.reason: Spring-catch assembly does not exercise threaded adjustment preservation.

comparisons.objective: Fit a long wardrobe rail into closed and open end supports under geometric constraints; candidate adjusts a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual long-part insertion and swing/tilt reorientation versus fine coaxial tool seating and jam-nut locking.
comparisons.success_condition: Both rail ends seated, level, still, and released versus accurate locked opening with low drift after three cycles.
comparisons.reason: Both are bimanual, but their tested geometries, force interactions, and terminal outcomes differ.

comparisons.objective: Thread two bauble hooks over narrow branches without breaking them; candidate locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Fragile suspended-object handling and hook-over-rod insertion versus rotary driver/wrench use and setting-preserving countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: Two ornaments hanging released and unbroken versus retained angular adjustment, installed nuts, repeated cycles, and clearance.
comparisons.reason: Precision placement is generic and does not establish ability-level overlap.

comparisons.objective: Fold a foil pan rim around a lid over its full perimeter; candidate locks a gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Progressive plastic folding while stabilizing lid and pan versus coaxial rotary adjustment and bimanual countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: All 24 rim sections folded with lid seated and hands clear versus retained locked angle after repeated articulated cycles.
comparisons.reason: Shared hold-and-work coordination is generic; perimeter crimping and threaded stop locking test different abilities.

comparisons.objective: Assemble a loose rack into a rack-and-pinion gripper at the correct tooth phase so both fingers open symmetrically; the candidate instead adjusts and locks an already-assembled gripper's opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1898 tests rack pickup, planar alignment, gear-tooth meshing, and symmetric jaw motion. The candidate tests coaxial driver seating, thin-jam-nut wrenching, and countertorque that preserves a screw setting.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1898 requires both racks seated, each jaw opened at least 15 mm, center error within 3 mm, and hands released for 1 s. The candidate requires a retained 90° opening within 3°, three repeat cycles, no more than 2° drift, retained nuts, and 30 mm clearance. No material rubric details are missing.
comparisons.reason: Although both concern gripper mechanisms and verify motion after manipulation, gear-phase assembly is meaningfully different from preserving an adjustable stop while locking a concentric jam nut against reaction torque.

comparisons.objective: Adjust a drum-brake star wheel until the drum has light drag; the candidate sets a gripper opening-stop screw to 90°, locks it, and verifies retained opening.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-2167 requires inserting and levering a brake spoon through a backing-plate slot, engaging successive teeth, regrasping, and turning the drum to assess drag. The candidate requires simultaneous hex-driver counterholding and thin-wrench tightening on a coupled screw and nut.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-2167 succeeds at 22–28 star-wheel clicks with light drag, spoon deposited, and hands clear for 1 s; overadjustment to lock scores 0. The candidate requires angle tolerance, nut retention, three close-open cycles, bounded drift, and tool clearance. No material rubric details are missing; PR-2167 discloses that shoe motion and drag are approximated from click count.
comparisons.reason: Both share the generic adjust-then-functionally-check pattern, but the brake task tests blind notched levering and drag judgment, whereas the candidate's defining ability is two-tool countertorque that prevents a screw setting from moving during locknut tightening.

comparisons.objective: Thread and tighten a spin-on oil filter to gasket contact and then to a prescribed turn or 18 N·m; the candidate adjusts and locks a gripper opening stop before cycling it.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1405 tests grasping and rotating a large threaded can, with later versions seating a cap wrench and applying ratchet torque. The candidate tests fine coaxial driver engagement plus a separate open-ended wrench on a thin nut while counterholding the adjustment screw.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1405 grades final rotation past gasket contact, penalizes loose, removed, or overcrushed filters, and requires release and wrench removal in later versions. The candidate grades retained 90° opening, nut retention, three motion cycles, drift, and clearance. No material rubric details are missing across the recorded versions.
comparisons.reason: Threaded tightening and tool release are shared primitives, but PR-1405 does not test preserving an independently adjustable stop against locknut reaction or validating that setting through repeated articulated cycles.

comparisons.objective: Align a suction tool plate with a robot quick-change flange and actuate its locking ring so the tool remains suspended; the candidate sets and locks an internal gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1054 tests carrying a tool, precise flange/dowel alignment, holding it seated, and operating a locking lever with the other hand. The candidate tests dual-tool coaxial seating and coordinated screw-versus-jam-nut countertorque, followed by operating a test lever.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1054 requires the correct tool seated and locked, the wrong tool never locked, hands clear, and arms returned; its versions specify dowel capture and ring-angle thresholds. The candidate requires a numeric opening angle, repeated retained motion, limited drift, hardware retention, and tool clearance. No material rubric details are missing.
comparisons.reason: Both involve bimanual stabilization during locking, but PR-1054 principally measures component alignment, insertion, and latch retention, while the candidate measures preservation of a calibrated rotational setting under tightening reaction and subsequent cycle stability.

comparisons.objective: Sweep test rods through two light-curtain fields, observe which curtain fails, and tag out that machine; the candidate mechanically adjusts and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-2070 tests controlled rod sweeping across complete sensing fields, maintaining orientation and speed, perceiving lamp state, and inserting a tag. The candidate tests precision driver and wrench use, countertorque, regrasping, and articulated verification.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-2070 requires all 45 cells of both fields covered, correct post-test tagging, rods withdrawn, release, stillness, and no dropped rod or tag. The candidate requires retained angular accuracy over three cycles with nuts retained and tools clear. No material rubric details are missing.
comparisons.reason: Safety-field coverage and fault-dependent tagging exercise inspection and decision-guided placement, not coupled screw adjustment, jam-nut locking, or retention of a mechanical calibration.

comparisons.objective: Roll puff pastry into an even 3 mm sheet at least 20 cm long; the candidate configures and locks a robot gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1694 tests coordinated rolling-pin control over deformable material, levelness, repeated passes, and safe set-down. The candidate tests small-tool seating, screw adjustment, wrench counterholding, and mechanism cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1694 grades sheet length, thickness uniformity, evenness, and final pin release, with partial credit for incomplete rolling. The candidate grades angle tolerance, lock and nut retention, repeated return accuracy, drift, and clearance. No material rubric details are missing, though PR-1694 explicitly uses a non-colliding scored dough approximation.
comparisons.reason: The tasks test unrelated abilities: distributed deformable-material thickness control versus localized coupled fastener adjustment and retained articulated calibration.

comparisons.objective: Activate a handheld 3D scanner and cover at least 95% of a cast housing's outer surface, including its top; the candidate adjusts and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-2016 tests button actuation, scanner handling at valid standoff and view angle, turntable coordination, occlusion planning, and tracking recovery. The candidate tests coaxial hand-tool use, countertorque, wrench regrasping, and mechanical cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-2016 requires 95% scan coverage, top coverage, final clearance, and no part disturbance, scanner collision, or drop. The candidate requires a retained 90° opening through three cycles with bounded drift and retained hardware. No material rubric details are missing; scanner facing and tracking limits are explicitly labeled assumptions.
comparisons.reason: Surface-view planning and noncontact inspection do not establish overlap with two-tool mechanical adjustment, locknut reaction control, or functional retention testing.

comparisons.objective: Place a pepper seedling plug, backfill it evenly, firm it, and leave it upright without damage; the candidate adjusts and locks a robot gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-2106 tests delicate plug handling, granular backfilling around a held object, support formation, and avoidance of stem or leaf damage. The candidate tests rigid hand-tool alignment, screw-and-nut countertorque, regrasping, and articulated verification.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-2106 grades plug depth and tilt, four-sided soil level, fill percentage, spill, firmness under a side push, release, and plant damage. The candidate grades opening angle, locking and retention, three-cycle return, drift, and tool clearance. No material rubric details are missing; the soil-clod and plant-damage approximations are disclosed.
comparisons.reason: Granular backfilling and damage-sensitive stabilization of a plant are meaningfully different from calibrated rigid-mechanism adjustment and locknut retention.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets and locks a robot-gripper opening stop, then verifies retained motion; PR-1941 fills and removes a vacuum blood tube while keeping a venipuncture needle stable.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires concentric driver/wrench seating, countertorque and locknut tightening; PR-1941 requires stabilizing a needle holder while pushing and pulling a tube.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a retained 90° setting, three repeatable cycles, lock retention and released clearance; PR-1941 requires tube filling and removal without needle displacement, followed by released tray placement.
comparisons.reason: Needle stabilization during tube exchange does not test preserving an adjustable screw setting against jam-nut reaction; all material rubric details are present.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks a robot-gripper stop before cycling it; PR-1766 clamps locking pliers onto a tube and leaves their latch supporting the tool.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses two coaxial tools for screw/nut countertorque and later actuates a mechanism; PR-1766 squeezes a handheld over-center substitute past its latch point while positioning its jaws.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires angular accuracy, limited drift over three cycles, retained nuts and clear tools; PR-1766 requires the released pliers to remain clamped at the marked height and orientation.
comparisons.reason: Both verify hands-off retention, but locking pliers test squeeze-to-latch clamping rather than counterholding a setting during locknut tightening; all material rubric details are present.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets a gripper opening stop and locks the adjustment; PR-2185 installs a mixer beater and guard, raises the bowl, and performs a guarded powered start-stop check.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires driver/wrench countertorque on coupled threaded parts; PR-2185 requires precise bayonet-style insertion, spring-collar compression, guard placement and control operation.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate succeeds on retained 90° opening over three cold cycles; PR-2185 succeeds on retained beater/guard assembly, lifted bowl, specified powered rotation and stopped endpoint.
comparisons.reason: Functional verification is shared only generically; bayonet tool installation and guarded motor operation do not test locknut-preserved stop adjustment, and no rubric details are missing.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks an angular gripper stop; PR-2258 squares a racked wooden face frame without moving it off its marks.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses coaxial tools and coordinated countertorque; PR-2258 applies opposed bimanual forces to rack a compliant four-joint frame while preventing gross sliding.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a locked angle and repeatable cycles; PR-2258 requires nearly equal diagonals, closed joints, location retention and released stillness.
comparisons.reason: Opposed-force coordination is generic, while the controlled mechanisms and measured outcomes are unrelated; all material rubric details are present.

comparisons.objective: Candidate preserves and locks one adjustable robot-gripper stop, then verifies motion; PR-1968 opens three breaker clamps, inserts a comb busbar and tightens all terminal screws.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires simultaneous driver counterholding and thin-nut tightening on one coupled adjustment; PR-1968 requires repeated screwdriver turning plus multi-pin alignment and insertion.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires retained angular calibration over three cycles; PR-1968 requires three inserted and tightened pins that resist a 10 N pull with hands and tool clear.
comparisons.reason: Both use a screwdriver, but terminal preparation and multi-pin busbar fastening do not test locking an adjustable screw without disturbing its setting; no rubric details are missing.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets and locks a gripper opening limit; PR-1151 purges air from a syringe while preserving liquid and returns it to a rack.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires tool seating, threaded countertorque and articulated verification; PR-1151 requires orienting a fluid-filled syringe, stabilizing its barrel and regulating plunger travel.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate measures retained angle, drift, nut retention and cycle function; PR-1151 measures residual air, liquid loss, safe pose, release and a continuous endpoint hold.
comparisons.reason: Fluid-preserving plunger control is meaningfully different from mechanical stop adjustment and locknut counterholding; all spec revisions provide sufficient rubric detail.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks a gripper stop; PR-1870 removes a drawer by operating two opposite-sense slide releases and sets it down.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses two coaxial tools for countertorque; PR-1870 simultaneously presses opposed latch levers while pulling and supporting a free drawer.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a retained 90° setting through three cycles; PR-1870 requires the drawer fully off both slides, flat, still and released on the table.
comparisons.reason: Bimanual coordination is shared only at a generic level; drawer unlatching and load removal do not test threaded setting preservation, and no rubric details are missing.

comparisons.objective: Candidate locks a robot-gripper opening adjustment and verifies it; PR-1951 performs the squeeze-turn-wait-and-withdraw step of a rapid strep test.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires driver/wrench seating and countertorque; PR-1951 maintains a moving squeeze on a soft tube while repeatedly regrasping and turning a swab.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires angular accuracy and low drift over cycles; PR-1951 requires five net turns, a timed dwell, continuously squeezed rotating withdrawal and disposal.
comparisons.reason: Maintaining deformable-tube squeeze during swab rotation and withdrawal is not the same ability as locknut-secured stop adjustment; all material rubric details are present.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks a robot-gripper opening stop; PR-125 aligns mating flanges and inserts locating pins.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires concentric threaded-tool counterholding; PR-125 requires holding flange faces and holes aligned while inserting horizontal pins.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate succeeds on a locked 90° setting retained through three cycles; PR-125 succeeds on flange-axis alignment and correctly seated pins.
comparisons.reason: Both involve bimanual assembly, but flange alignment and pin insertion do not test preserving a threaded adjustment during jam-nut locking; no rubric details are missing.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets and locks a gripper opening stop; PR-1302 unzips an ESD bag, extracts one battery and seats it upright while leaving the other inside.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires tool regrasping and coordinated screw/nut torque; PR-1302 requires zipper manipulation, selective extraction and orientation-sensitive placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires retained angular function over repeated cycles; PR-1302 requires the bag opened, one cell seated positive-up, the other retained, and both arms returned.
comparisons.reason: Selective unpacking and battery placement have no meaningful adjustment-locking or countertorque requirement; all material rubric details are present.

comparisons.objective: Candidate locks an adjusted robot-gripper stop; PR-1868 connects a hose nipple to a sprung quick-connect coupler.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate counterholds a screw while tightening its jam nut; PR-1868 retracts a sprung collar while aligning and inserting a flexible-hose fitting, then releases it to latch.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires retained angle and repeatable articulated motion; PR-1868 requires seated pawl engagement, collar return, pull retention, stillness and hand clearance.
comparisons.reason: Both culminate in hands-off retention, but quick-connect insertion under collar spring load does not test locknut preservation of an adjustable setting; no rubric details are missing.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks a gripper stop; PR-685 drives a wing corkscrew into a cork and extracts it while the bottle remains in its cradle.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses a hex driver and thin wrench for coupled countertorque; PR-685 performs helical insertion followed by lever-powered high-force extraction and bottle stabilization.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a stable 90° opening across cycles; PR-685 requires the cork fully removed and displaced while the bottle stays within cradle-motion limits.
comparisons.reason: Shared rotary tool use is generic; cork penetration and extraction do not test locknut tightening without calibration drift, and all rubric details are present.

comparisons.objective: Candidate mechanically calibrates and locks a gripper opening stop; PR-996 calibrates a colorimeter with a blank and measures a sealed sample at a requested wavelength.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires physical screw/nut countertorque and mechanism actuation; PR-996 requires cuvette identification, optical-face alignment, device-button operation and ordered reference measurement.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires angle retention through repeated cycles; PR-996 requires a valid blank reference, accurate sample reading, and both cuvettes returned released and still.
comparisons.reason: The word calibration describes different tested abilities: optical reference workflow versus force-coupled mechanical adjustment; all material rubric details are present.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks a gripper stop; PR-1444 sets a spring rat trap without allowing a snap or exposing a gripper to the strike path.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate applies coordinated threaded countertorque; PR-1444 restrains a spring-loaded hammer while positioning and latching a separate lock bar.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires retained angle over three cycles with tools clear; PR-1444 requires the hammer latched back, no snap or unsafe strike-path exposure, and arms clear.
comparisons.reason: Both coordinate against a reaction load, but trap setting tests spring restraint and hazard-aware latching rather than locknut-preserved adjustment; no rubric details are missing.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets and locks a robot-gripper motion limit; PR-1849 gauges seven machined blocks and sorts them by dimensional tolerance.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires coaxial tool seating and countertorque; PR-1849 requires repeated alignment with GO and NO-GO gaps, released gauge checks and sorting.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a retained target angle and functional cycles; PR-1849 requires valid ordered gauge checks and correct final tray classification, with escapes penalized.
comparisons.reason: Dimensional inspection and classification do not test threaded stop locking or retention under cycling; all material rubric details are present.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks a gripper opening stop; PR-1935 couples a scaffold transom by positioning it, closing a cap, swinging a bolt and running down its nut.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate must counterhold an adjustment screw while tightening a concentric jam nut; PR-1935 supports and aligns a long tube, operates a hinged cap and bolt, and spins a single fastening nut.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires preserved angle and repeated motion after release; PR-1935 requires the transom on its mark, square, capped, bolted, gripped and hands clear.
comparisons.reason: Running down a scaffold fastener does not require preserving a calibrated screw position against its locknut or verifying retained articulated travel; no rubric details are missing.

comparisons.objective: Candidate calibrates and locks an angular gripper stop; PR-2015 turns a suspended humanoid upper body half a revolution and brings it gently to rest.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses precise two-tool countertorque and later cycles a mechanism; PR-2015 regulates the momentum of a freely yawing 18.3 kg suspended assembly through push and catch actions.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a locked 90° opening with low drift over three cycles; PR-2015 requires approximately 180° net rotation, under 1°/s for one second, without blows or collisions.
comparisons.reason: Both concern robot hardware, but suspended-load momentum control is a different tested ability from threaded stop adjustment; all material rubric details are present.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks a robot-gripper stop; PR-1276 reloads a spring-return long-arm stapler and staples two sheets.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires simultaneous driver and wrench control; PR-1276 holds a sprung magazine open, inserts and seats a staple strip, handles paper and presses the stapler.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires angular retention and repeatable cycles; PR-1276 requires the stapler loaded, sheets physically stapled together, mechanisms still and arms clear.
comparisons.reason: Holding a magazine open during loading and subsequently firing a staple does not test preserving a screw adjustment during jam-nut locking; no rubric details are missing.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets and locks a gripper opening stop; PR-1956 breaks a cocktail-shaker seal and separates the tins without spilling.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires concentric driver-and-wrench countertorque that preserves an angular setting; PR-1956 requires holding one tin and delivering a correctly placed impact before lifting the other.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a locked 90° setting, limited drift, three repeatable cycles, retained hardware, and released clearance; PR-1956 requires blow-caused seal release, separated upright tins, clear hands, and no dent, spill, or loss.
comparisons.reason: Placed impact and spill-safe vessel separation do not test coupled screw adjustment, locknut reaction control, or post-lock functional retention; both rubrics provide material numeric details.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks a gripper stop at 90°; PR-2142 opens a keyless drill chuck, removes its bit, and deposits the bit in a tray.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both involve bimanual reaction control, but the candidate must keep a driver seated while a concentric jam nut is tightened without rotating the adjusted screw; PR-2142 counterholds a loose drill while hand-turning its sleeve, then extracts the bit.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate scores retained angle and repeated articulated cycles after both tools are withdrawn; PR-2142 scores the bit wholly outside the chuck, safely supported or tray-contained, with the drill and objects released and still.
comparisons.reason: PR-2142 tests chuck release and extraction, not preservation of a calibrated screw phase against its locknut's tightening reaction or subsequent motion verification; no material rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets and locks an angular-gripper stop; PR-741 inserts a stripped cable into a lug, actuates a crimping press, removes the terminated cable, and returns it to its rest.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires two concentric tools and countertorque during locking; PR-741 requires depth-and-axis-controlled cable insertion held while another hand closes a lever press.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires retained 90° opening over three cycles with low drift and retained nuts; PR-741 requires prescribed insertion depth and alignment at crimp, release, removal, rest placement, and in later versions a real pull test.
comparisons.reason: Holding an inserted cable while operating a crimper does not test locking a continuous adjustment against coupled jam-nut torque or retained articulated motion; all spec versions state observable criteria.

comparisons.objective: Candidate calibrates and locks a gripper opening stop; PR-984 centers an inside-bolt-circle gasket between flanges and inserts four bolts.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate emphasizes coaxial tool seating, wrench regrasping, and countertorque; PR-984 emphasizes planar gasket insertion and centering in a constrained gap followed by repeated bolt-through-hole placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires locked angle retention and repeatable close-open cycles; PR-984 requires the gasket centered and flat, the upper flange undisturbed, all four bolts seated through both flanges, release, and dwell.
comparisons.reason: Gasket alignment and multi-bolt insertion do not exercise coupled adjustment-and-locking reaction control; the absence of modeled threads or torque in PR-984 further separates the tested ability, and its rubric is detailed.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets and locks a gripper stop; PR-1209 flush-cuts a circuit-board lead while retaining and disposing of the offcut safely.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses simultaneous driver and wrench control on coupled threaded elements; PR-1209 requires nipper alignment and closure while the other gripper captures a small offcut to prevent free flight.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate scores angle accuracy, lock retention, repeated cycles, and clearance; PR-1209 scores flushness and offcut disposition, with zero for unsafe free flight and full credit for released placement in the scrap cup.
comparisons.reason: Safe cutting and projectile capture are materially different from preserving a mechanical setpoint during jam-nut tightening and validating it through actuation; all versions specify the relevant thresholds.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks a robot-gripper opening limit; PR-1896 reads tire pressure through a Schrader valve with a pencil gauge and returns the gauge to its holder.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires concentric two-tool torque coordination; PR-1896 requires square axial gauge seating, controlled valve-core depression, a timed seal, and replacement of the gauge.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a retained angular setting over three cycles; PR-1896 requires a sealed 1.5-second press, a 33–37 psi stick reading, upright holder placement, release, and stillness.
comparisons.reason: Pressure-gauge sealing and reading do not test locking an adjustable stop against fastening reaction or post-lock articulated repeatability; no material rubric details are missing.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets and locks a gripper opening stop; PR-1906 performs an insulin-pen safety shot and then dials a 12-unit dose.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses a hex driver and thin-nut wrench with coordinated countertorque; PR-1906 requires cap removal, repeated dose-knob regrasping, visual unit correction, axial injection-force control, and safe needle orientation.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires retained 90° opening through three cycles; PR-1906 requires a completed 2-unit safety shot with the needle up and a five-second hold, then a displayed 12-unit setting, safe tray placement, and clearance.
comparisons.reason: Dose dialing and priming a medical pen are not equivalent to coupled screw-and-locknut calibration or functional retention testing; the record supplies numeric outcome and safety criteria.

comparisons.objective: Candidate calibrates and locks an angular gripper; PR-2019 scrapes bonded char from a griddle into its grease tray.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires precision tool seating and torque counterholding; PR-2019 requires maintaining a scraper-edge attitude, applying lateral force to break debris bonds, overlapping strokes, and controlling material flow.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate scores angle accuracy, hardware retention, cycles, drift, and release; PR-2019 scores debris mass transferred to the tray, cleanliness, scraper set-down, and penalties for off-griddle debris or gouging.
comparisons.reason: Surface scraping and debris containment test forceful planar tool use rather than coupled threaded adjustment and retained mechanism calibration; the scoring rubric is complete and quantitative.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks a gripper stop; PR-2259 loads a lancet into a lancing device, removes its tab, replaces the cap, and cocks the device.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires simultaneous driver-and-wrench countertorque; PR-2259 requires cap removal, small-part axial insertion, twist-off separation, snap fitting, spring cocking, and avoiding an exposed needle.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires retained angle over repeated gripper cycles; PR-2259 requires the lancet home, tab removed, cap snapped on, device cocked and laid down, with zero for needle proximity or device loss.
comparisons.reason: The lancet task is a sequential small-device assembly and sharps-safety procedure, not preservation of a continuous setting under concentric locknut reaction; its rubric states all material thresholds.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets and locks a robot-gripper opening stop; PR-2260 packs a rolled poster into a mailing tube and seats an end cap at each end.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires coaxial driver and wrench manipulation with countertorque; PR-2260 requires long-object alignment and insertion, tube stabilization, and coaxial press-fitting of two caps.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a locked 90° setting, three repeatable cycles, retained nuts, and clearance; PR-2260 requires the roll sufficiently inside, one or both caps geometrically seated, hands off, stillness, real-world cap retention, and no poster damage.
comparisons.reason: Long-roll packing and friction-cap insertion do not test coupled adjustment locking or articulated setting retention; no material success-condition detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks a gripper opening stop; PR-793 fits a rubber stopper at least 12 mm onto a glass tube while safely supporting the tube.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both use two hands against reaction, but the candidate controls two concentric threaded elements with separate tools to prevent locknut-induced setpoint rotation; PR-793 grips fragile glass close to the work while pushing and twisting an interference-fit stopper.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires angular accuracy, seated retained nuts, tool withdrawal, three repeatable cycles, and low drift; PR-793 requires insertion depth and release, with zero for unsupported working or glass damage.
comparisons.reason: Safe support during interference insertion does not subsume preservation of a calibrated threaded setting against its own locking torque and subsequent functional cycling; all versions expose the relevant safety and depth criteria.

comparisons.objective: Candidate sets and locks a gripper opening limit; PR-2256 measures brake-rotor thickness with a handheld outside micrometer and preserves the reading after removal.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires hex-driver and jam-nut-wrench countertorque; PR-2256 requires positioning a micrometer on a friction band, keeping it square, rocking for the minimum, and turning a ratchet to controlled measuring force.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires a retained 90° gripper opening through three cycles; PR-2256 requires a reading within ±0.02 mm, two ratchet clicks, reading retention off the rotor, and released placement on the rest.
comparisons.reason: Although both retain a setting, PR-2256 tests metrological contact and reading preservation, not locking a mechanical adjustment against coupled fastening reaction or verifying articulated function; its rubric is numeric.

comparisons.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks a gripper opening stop; PR-892 loads a filled syringe into a pump, seats its flange, advances the driver gently, and in later versions closes the barrel clamp.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires concentric driver-and-wrench torque coordination; PR-892 requires syringe alignment and insertion, flange-slot seating, clamp articulation, and force-limited driver placement without moving the plunger.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires retained angle, hardware retention, repeated cycles, and released clearance; PR-892 requires a seated and clamped syringe, driver flush to the plunger, no plunger displacement, stillness, and a one-second hold.
comparisons.reason: Gentle medical-device loading and no-dose contact control do not test continuous stop adjustment, jam-nut reaction counterholding, or post-lock motion retention; the record's versions provide detailed thresholds.

comparisons.objective: Prune a dead rose cane above a live bud, retain the cutting, and place it in a bin without harming the plant.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual secateur operation with precise cut placement and continuous control of a freed offcut.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct 3–15 mm stub, intact bud, cutting in bin, tool and hands released; green-cane cutting, dropping, or plant damage revokes credit.
comparisons.reason: The candidate tests concentric driver-and-wrench countertorque, retained stop calibration, and post-lock cycling, not cutting and controlling an offcut.

comparisons.objective: Load a caulking gun and apply a continuous silicone bead along a bath joint.
comparisons.physical_skill: Operate a release and plunger, seat a cartridge, meter the trigger, and guide a nozzle along a seam.
comparisons.success_condition: Credit follows cartridge loading and joint coverage; full credit requires at least 95% sealed with no gap over 2 mm and the gun released.
comparisons.reason: Its coupled actions load and dispense material, whereas the candidate preserves a screw-set angular stop while tightening a jam nut and verifies retention by cycling.

comparisons.objective: Push a loaded tote down a passive roller conveyor so it reaches a remote station without a damaging end-stop impact.
comparisons.physical_skill: Regulate release velocity and momentum while keeping a loose bottle stable.
comparisons.success_condition: The tote must stop at or near the station; bottle tipping, excessive impact speed, lifting, or prohibited robot reach causes zero.
comparisons.reason: Ballistic release-speed control on a conveyor does not test coaxial tool seating, locknut counterholding, or retained mechanism calibration.

comparisons.objective: Move a tissue-roll stub to the reserve spindle, install a new primary roll, set the changeover shutter, and close the dispenser.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold release buttons while extracting and seating large cores, then manipulate a shutter and sprung cover.
comparisons.success_condition: Credit requires correctly engaged rolls in their assigned hubs, a latched cover, correct shutter position, and released hands; misassignment and unsafe closure fail.
comparisons.reason: This tests release-controlled core transfer and dispenser sequencing, not preserving an adjustable screw setting against jam-nut reaction or validating repeated motion.

comparisons.objective: Seat four wired connector modules in a sprung hinged frame and close it until latched.
comparisons.physical_skill: Repeated tight-clearance insertion of adjacent modules followed by closure without dislodging them.
comparisons.success_condition: Full credit requires all four modules seated within millimetre tolerances, frame clicked shut, hands clear, and a one-second hold; dropped or crushed modules fail.
comparisons.reason: Multi-part insertion and sprung-frame latching are meaningfully different from two-tool countertorque calibration and hands-off cycle retention.

comparisons.objective: Reset tongue-and-groove pliers from the narrowest to the widest groove and leave them locked.
comparisons.physical_skill: Open past a release angle, translate a slip joint along its slot, then close it into a discrete groove.
comparisons.success_condition: Full credit requires groove 5 locked, pliers flat and still, and hands clear for one second; intermediate grooves receive partial credit.
comparisons.reason: Although both change and retain an opening, this record tests release-angle-gated sliding into a discrete groove, while the candidate tests continuous screw adjustment preserved through jam-nut countertorque and three functional cycles.

comparisons.objective: Seal, shake, and reopen a Boston cocktail shaker without spilling its contents.
comparisons.physical_skill: Create and break a press fit, execute vigorous bimanual oscillation, and contain loose contents.
comparisons.success_condition: Credit depends on sufficient sealed shaking or mixing, limited spill, reopening, and returning the large tin upright; an unsealed tipped shaker fails.
comparisons.reason: Press-fit containment and dynamic shaking do not exercise calibrated screw adjustment, wrench/driver counterholding, or retained angular-stop verification.

comparisons.objective: Measure a standing pin with a handheld digital caliper and return the caliper to its rest.
comparisons.physical_skill: Align jaws squarely, close them with very low force, stabilize a reading, and release the instrument.
comparisons.success_condition: Accuracy, angular alignment, jaw force, contact on both jaws, final placement, clearance, and stillness determine credit.
comparisons.reason: Both involve precision, but caliper metrology tests gentle bilateral contact and reading accuracy, not mechanically locking a setting against tightening torque and cycling it.

comparisons.objective: Fully unfold a passive laptop stand and seat both support rods in its highest slots inside a marked area.
comparisons.physical_skill: Coordinate a scissor linkage and insert two support rods into separate detents.
comparisons.success_condition: Independent credit covers full spread and each rod; full credit additionally requires both rails supported, outline inside the rectangle, and release.
comparisons.reason: This is articulated unfolding and dual rod seating; it has no threaded adjustment, coupled locknut reaction, or repeated-motion retention test. The rubric does not numerically define “full spread” or gripper-clear distance, but that omission does not create plausible overlap.

comparisons.objective: Fit a spring tension rod level between cupboard walls at a marked height so it supports itself.
comparisons.physical_skill: Compress and align a telescoping sprung rod while establishing frictional contact at both ends.
comparisons.success_condition: The released rod must press both walls, remain still and clear of the table, meet height/level/square limits, and hold full conditions for four seconds.
comparisons.reason: Spring compression and frictional placement between walls do not test tool-mediated stop calibration, jam-nut countertorque, or functional cycling.

comparisons.objective: Turn and place a brad nailer into its case without pointing it at a coworker or touching the trigger.
comparisons.physical_skill: Safety-constrained rigid-tool reorientation, possibly with a bimanual handoff.
comparisons.success_condition: Any unsafe pointing or finger-trigger proximity causes zero; credit otherwise depends on final placement, release, and stillness.
comparisons.reason: Its tested ability is hazard-aware reorientation along a safe path, unrelated to coupled threaded adjustment and retention verification.

comparisons.objective: Remove a jammed card from a printer without tearing it, put it down, and resume printing.
comparisons.physical_skill: Apply balanced bimanual extraction forces at both card edges, then operate a button.
comparisons.success_condition: Credit tracks extraction and placement; seam shear of 1.5 mm causes irrevocable zero, and full credit requires the OK press, clearance, and one-second stillness.
comparisons.reason: Balanced extraction of a fragile sheet tests symmetric pulling and tear avoidance, not countertorque between concentric tools or preservation of a calibrated stop.

comparisons.objective: Seat and tighten a positive battery cable clamp on its tapered post with correct cable orientation.
comparisons.physical_skill: Align a spring-loaded clamp, seat it fully, and torque one pinch nut with a wrench.
comparisons.success_condition: Full credit requires seating, 5–7 N·m nut torque, lug alignment, safe wrench placement, hand clearance, and stillness; high, crooked, misplaced, or moved assemblies fail.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest threaded-tool record, but it tightens one clamp nut to a torque after seating; the candidate uniquely requires simultaneous driver counterholding to preserve a continuous stop setting and repeated articulated-cycle retention.

comparisons.objective: Add a personal padlock through a free group-lockout hasp hole without disturbing a coworker’s lock or enabling the switch.
comparisons.physical_skill: Align and insert a shackle through two hasp jaws, close its latch, and avoid disturbing an existing safety assembly.
comparisons.success_condition: Full credit requires the closed lock to withstand hasp-pry and handle-on tests after release; moving the coworker’s lock or opening/turning the mechanism early causes irrevocable zero.
comparisons.reason: Shackle insertion and safety interlocking do not involve threaded calibration, reaction counterholding, or verification of a retained angular stop.

comparisons.objective: Push a shower-valve cartridge fully home against O-ring resistance and install its U-shaped retaining clip.
comparisons.physical_skill: Maintain axial force and angular alignment with one hand while inserting a close-clearance clip with the other.
comparisons.success_condition: Full credit requires the cartridge flush and square, clip fully seated, retention under a 20 N pull, hands clear, and a one-second hold; a dropped clip fails.
comparisons.reason: It shares genuine bimanual stabilization, but tests simultaneous press-and-clip insertion against spring-back, not two-tool screw/nut countertorque, target-angle preservation, and repeated cycling.

comparisons.objective: Spin wet lettuce in a hand-crank salad spinner at drying speed while keeping the loose lid and bowl stable.
comparisons.physical_skill: Continuously crank a moving knob while the other hand restrains a reaction-loaded bowl and lid.
comparisons.success_condition: Credit depends on basket speed above 300 rpm for specified durations and final crank release; excessive base motion, tilt, or lid displacement causes zero.
comparisons.reason: Bimanual reaction restraint is generic overlap only; sustained cranking and lid stability do not test precision stop adjustment, jam-nut locking, or drift after cycles.

comparisons.objective: Shake a separatory funnel to mix two layers, periodically vent it safely, and return it to its support.
comparisons.physical_skill: Control a stoppered vessel during vigorous oscillation while reorienting and operating a stopcock to manage pressure.
comparisons.success_condition: Stroke count and safe venting determine credit; overpressure, unsafe valve orientation, or loss of contents fails, while full credit requires 12 strokes and stable released placement.
comparisons.reason: The task tests hazardous vessel shaking and periodic pressure relief, not calibrated threaded adjustment, coupled locking, or retained articulated motion.

comparisons.objective: Cut marked copper tubing without denting or spiraling the cut; candidate instead sets and locks a gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Repeatedly feed and orbit a tubing cutter with handoffs; no jam-nut counterholding that preserves an angular setting.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires controlled groove depth, completed cut, roundness, mark accuracy, and release; candidate requires retained 90° opening across three cycles.
comparisons.reason: Both use tools and rotational control, but the tested mechanisms and outcomes—progressive cutting versus lock-preserved stop adjustment—are meaningfully different.

comparisons.objective: Mix flour and liquid into dough while stabilizing a loose bowl; candidate adjusts and locks a mechanical gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Stabilize a vessel while sweeping a spoon through granular ingredients; no coaxial driver/wrench coupling or setting retention.
comparisons.success_condition: Scores mixed-flour share while penalizing tipping and material loss; candidate scores opening angle, locked retention, cycling, and clearance.
comparisons.reason: Shared bimanual stabilization is generic; mixing distributed material does not test countertorque locking of an adjustable stop.

comparisons.objective: Rotate a long parcel in confined space and push it into a bay; candidate configures a gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Coordinated opposing pushes for in-place carton rotation, followed by translation; no fastener engagement or counterholding.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires correct parcel orientation and placement without moving neighboring boxes; candidate requires a locked 90° setting retained through actuation.
comparisons.reason: The parcel task tests constrained whole-object reorientation, not coupled screw-and-jam-nut adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Pry a press-fit paint-tin lid free and place it safely; candidate sets and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Insert a screwdriver into a rim groove, lever successive lid regions, and reorient the tin; no simultaneous wrench/driver countertorque.
comparisons.success_condition: Scores partial lid release, full removal, safe orientation, placement, and release; candidate scores angular accuracy and retained function after locking.
comparisons.reason: Tool use is shared, but distributed prying of a lid tests a different contact mechanism and outcome from preserving a threaded adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Pour an accurate 10 mL syrup dose while holding a cup level, then place both vessels; candidate adjusts a mechanical stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Coordinated vessel holding, flow-rate control, and precise pour termination; no threaded adjustment or locking reaction.
comparisons.success_condition: Scores dose volume, spill, observability, placement, and settling; candidate scores locked opening angle and repeatable cycles.
comparisons.reason: Precision pouring and spill control are unrelated to two-tool setting preservation despite both requiring bimanual coordination.

comparisons.objective: Remove a drone prop nut, replace the propeller, and retighten the nut; candidate adjusts and locks a gripper opening stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold a freely rotating propeller while turning one nut, remove and insert parts, then tighten; candidate counterholds an adjustment screw while tightening its concentric jam nut.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires the nut to come off, the old propeller to be binned, the new one seated, and the nut tightened; candidate requires a 90° setting retained through three cycles.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest shared primitive of resisting rotation during nut turning, but propeller replacement does not test preserving an adjustable setting against jam-nut reaction or verifying retained articulated motion.

comparisons.objective: Fit and hand-tighten a keyed oxygen regulator yoke on a cylinder; candidate sets and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Blind pin alignment, yoke seating, and holding the assembly square while turning a T-screw; no driver-held adjustment screw beneath a jam nut.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires pin insertion, washer alignment, clamp torque, release, and stability; candidate requires angular accuracy, lock retention, and repeated actuation.
comparisons.reason: Although both combine stabilization with screw tightening, the regulator tests keyed insertion and clamp formation rather than preserving a pre-set screw position during locknut tightening.

comparisons.objective: Hand-guide a Franka arm to a service pose while correctly holding an enabling switch, then teach the pose; candidate mechanically configures a gripper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Continuous force-guiding of a seven-joint arm while maintaining a three-position safety control in its enable band.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires pose accuracy, correct button state, Teach actuation, collision avoidance, and clearance; candidate requires a locked opening angle retained over cycles.
comparisons.reason: Robot setup relevance is shared, but hand-guiding with an enabling device tests a different physical ability from mechanical stop adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Hang steel plates on moving conveyor hooks before a deadline; candidate adjusts and locks a stationary gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Track moving hooks and thread small plate holes while controlling swing and release timing.
comparisons.success_condition: Scores extraction, hook insertion, and freely settled hanging before the hook crosses a mark; candidate scores angle, lock retention, cycling, and clearance.
comparisons.reason: Dynamic target tracking and hanging do not exercise coupled fastener countertorque or retained adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Unscrew capped needles from syringes without exposing sharps and deposit them in a container; candidate sets and locks a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold a syringe against thread drag while turning and axially removing a small capped needle; no jam-nut locking or preservation of a calibrated setting.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires capped needle removal and disposal, with any cap loss causing failure; candidate requires retained angle and functional cycling.
comparisons.reason: Both resist reaction torque during threaded manipulation, but safe component removal is not the candidate's coupled adjustment-and-locking ability.

comparisons.objective: Retrieve an out-of-reach jar by pulling its supporting board, then place it in a basket; candidate configures a gripper stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Infer and execute indirect support manipulation followed by grasp-and-place.
comparisons.success_condition: Scores bringing the jar into reach and ultimately releasing it in the basket without loss; candidate scores locked angular setting and repeated motion.
comparisons.reason: Indirect retrieval has no meaningful mechanical or outcome overlap with two-tool stop adjustment.

last_candidate.title: Set and lock a robot gripper opening stop, then verify retained motion
last_candidate.objective: On an unpressurized, already-assembled representative SCHUNK DRG 80 bench fixture, adjust the opening-stop screw to a declared 90° total opening, lock it without changing the setting, withdraw both tools, and operate a cold test lever to verify retained opening over repeated cycles.
skills: open-ended wrench seating on a thin jam nut
coupled screw adjustment and nut locking
last_candidate.success_conditions: Initial score is 0. Award 0.25 for a released opening within 6° of the declared 90° target; 0.5 when within 3° with nut 73 seated against the cover and nut 74 retained in its modeled installed position; 0.75 when both tools are removed and one close-open cycle returns within 3°; 1.0 after three cycles each return within 3°, stop drift is at most 2°, both nuts remain retained, and tools and robot grippers remain at least 30 mm clear for one second. Revoke angle and cycle credit whenever locking, retention, or clearance prerequisites fail. A missing screw or nut, a dropped or inaccessible tool, fixture displacement, non-finite state, or motion outside the modeled 20°–180° range scores 0. Equivalent safe strategies earn the same outcome score; arm identity, order, path, action count, and impulse windows are not graded. The target, tolerances, cycle count, and clearance are explicit benchmark assumptions checkable by protractor, witness marks, nut-gap inspection, and video.
last_candidate.industrial_value: SCHUNK specifies opening-angle adjustment, locking, and pneumatic functional testing for its DRG 44–80 industrial grippers, making this direct robot-end-effector setup work within Impact on AI timelines. Its tested ability differs from generic tightening and the accepted hose-clamp task: the robot must preserve an adjustable stop against locknut reaction and then demonstrate hands-off functional retention. It also differs from PR 1540 because two concentric tools act on a coupled screw-and-nut setting rather than stabilizing a sensor body during connector assembly, and from PR 2229 because no third-body feeler gauge or cam clamp establishes the target.
last_candidate.dexterity: One gripper must keep a driver seated in the adjustment screw while the other seats and turns a wrench on nut 73. Tightening must physically tend to disturb an unrestrained screw, requiring coordinated countertorque, angular regulation, possible wrench regrasping, clean tool withdrawal, and subsequent operation of the articulated test fixture.

last_candidate.asset_plan: Build independently authored, full-scale representative rigid geometry, not a redistributed SCHUNK CAD model. Preserve the catalog drawing’s dimensional semantics: 100 × 71.6 × 135.5 mm are catalog X/Y/Z reference dimensions, not a claimed bounding envelope, and the page-7 drawing separately shows a 183.35 mm extent to point P. Represent the anodized-aluminum housing, steel angular jaws, native revolute jaw joints, common centric coupling, accessible adjustment screw, nut 73 as the locking nut, and retained nut 74 as the second manufacturer-specified nut; its precise spacing and role beyond installation are disclosed fixture assumptions because the manual does not explain them. Provide real hex and wrench contact geometry and a native or conservative task-local torque/friction mechanism in which tightening disturbs an unrestrained screw. The cold lever replaces pneumatic actuation only for bench verification. Target angle, hardware dimensions absent from the manual, friction, preload, and tolerances remain declared assumptions. Before demo development, validate reset, tool seating, restrained-versus-unrestrained causality, joint traces, loss cases, release clearance, and timestep sensitivity in the pinned Isaac Sim 6.1/YAM runtime.
last_candidate.risk: Closest ability-level neighbors include PR 1540, PR 1799, PR 1865, PR 2018, PR 2167, and PR 2229. Novelty depends on retaining genuine concentric two-tool screw/nut countertorque and functional-cycle verification; an implementation with zero driver reaction or a scripted phase flag would collapse into existing stabilization or adjustment tasks. No current native gripper trial exists, so implementation feasibility and physics validation remain future gates rather than claimed evidence.
